A `storage=` source whose stored table had a column outside Malloy's basic types (a list such as `INTEGER[]`, a struct, a MAP, BLOB, INTERVAL, ENUM, UNION or JSON column, or a list of structs) was never stored. Its build failed after the table was written, with 422 and the message "cannot be served from its storage destination: its materialized shape does not compile in DuckDB (… 'json' is a reserved word …)", the table was dropped, and the source answered every query live. The build-time check declared each such column as `json`, which Malloy does not accept in a type declaration. A chained `storage=` source over such a parent never built over the parent's table either: it recomputed from the warehouse, or was refused under `strictUpstreams`. Present in 0.13.0 and earlier.

To tell whether you were affected, look for a failed materialization run whose `error` names `'json' is a reserved word`, or a non-zero `publisher_materialization_eligibility_refused_total` with `reason="not_duckdb_portable"`.

Now the build declares a list or struct column as Malloy's array or record type, and leaves out of the declaration a column Malloy has no faithful type for, rather than refusing the table. A query reading a left-out column is answered live, with the same answer as before; every other query reads the stored table. A chained build over such a parent builds over its table. Rerun the failed materializations, or wait for the next scheduled run, and these tables now build and serve. A table with no column left to declare is still refused: the failure on its run record names those columns by name and type (never by value), and the build's `materialization.build.failed` log event carries code `not_duckdb_portable`. The served copy declares each stored list or struct in the shape live answers it in (a list of zoned timestamps as `timestamptz[]`), and leaves it out, so a query reading it is answered live, when no declaration reads it back as live does: a field live types as a warehouse-native type, or one holding such a value or an integer that live keeps exact past 2^53 (a `BIGINT[]` on DuckDB, say), which a declared `number` would round. One consequence on DuckDB: a persisted `nest:` whose rows hold a BIGINT field (a nest grouped by a BIGINT id, or one that sums a BIGINT) is now answered live when a query reads the nest, where it was served and rounded past 2^53; queries that do not read the nest are still served. No API change.

**Columns a `storage=` table served in another type or text than live now answer live.** Present in 0.13.0 and earlier, on any `storage=` source, `#@ persist` or `#(materialize)`:

- A column live types as a warehouse-native type (`sql native`): a `uuid` from Postgres or DuckDB, and a Postgres `json`, `jsonb` or composite type, which the destination stores as text. The stored table declared each a `string`, so the result schema differed from live's, and for the Postgres text columns the value did too (live's `{"n":1}` was served as `{"n": 1}`, a composite `{"a":1,"b":"p"}` as `(1,p)`). Decided from the type live gives the field.
- A Postgres `bytea` or `interval`, which Malloy types `string` and live answers in Postgres's own text (`\x0102`, `3 mons`). The build cast them to text DuckDB writes differently (`\x01\x02`, `3 months`). The build now keeps them as the BLOB and INTERVAL the destination reads them as, decided from the column types the destination's session reports for the source query before anything is stored, never from a value.

Each such column is left out of the stored table's declaration: a query reading it (a `select: *` included) is answered live, and every other query still reads the table. A `#(materialize)` source that reaches such a field through an inlined join answers live as a whole. A `#(materialize) storage=` table also declares a zoned timestamp `timestamptz`, as live types it, where it said `timestamp`.

To tell whether you were affected: a `storage=` source with a column of one of those types, queried by that column. The `uuid`, `json`, `jsonb` and composite columns are corrected on upgrade with no rebuild. A `bytea` or `interval` column is corrected when its table is next rebuilt in full: a table built before the upgrade holds the old text, and nothing on it says the column was once a `bytea`, so it keeps serving that text until then (an incremental table until it is re-seeded). Rebuild those sources with `forceRefresh`.

## [0.13.0] — A `storage=` table is served only to the definition that built it

A wrong answer is fixed. A `storage=` manifest entry whose content address (`sourceEntityId`) none of the package's sources has was still served to the one source of its name. In an unversioned package, an author who edited a `#@ persist storage=` source under its old name and restarted (which restores the latest run's tables), or bound a host manifest from before the edit, was answered from the old definition's rows. Such an entry now serves nothing, and the source answers live until its own table is built, as a colocated table and every published version already were. Every entry Publisher writes carries the address it computes, so a manifest it built for the current definition is unaffected.

## [0.13.0] — The v1 cutover is the only path: `PUBLISHER_V1_SERVED_COPY` is removed

The storage serve shape, the `#@ preaggregate` composite and the build manifest on the live compile are retired (materialization v2's v1 cutover, step 6g). v1 `#@ persist` tables are read only by the served copy and v1 `#@ preaggregate` rollups only by the rollup leg, as with the default `on` since the previous section, and a query reads a table only when its path report says so. `PUBLISHER_V1_SERVED_COPY` is no longer read: a deployment that sets it, `off` or `shadow` included, gets the cutover's paths, with no warning, so remove it from your configuration. The shadow comparison and its metric `publisher_v1_served_copy_shadow_total` are gone, and so is `publisher_storage_serve_shape_tier_drop_total`, which only the serve shape counted. `publisher_storage_bindings_withheld_total` is now counted by the served copy, and `publisher_storage_serve_shape_type_fallback_total` keeps its name (the build still counts it). No composite companion is compiled at load, so a build plan's `omittedSources` no longer reports `preaggregate_companion_failed`; a v1 rollup the rollup companion fails to plan is `rollup_companion_failed`. A dry run's per-view preview compiles each view against the served copy: a view it cannot compile is `live` with its own compile error, and a source the served copy cannot re-root has every view `live` with the reason, where the serve shape searched for the view at fault by halving. `PUBLISHER_MATERIALIZE_GATED_SOURCES` alone decides whether a gated table is read; a gated v1 `#@ persist storage=` source stays live even with it on, since it is refused at build (`persist-source-refused`, reason `authorize`) and has no table. The conformance runner (`scripts/v1-cutover-conformance.ts`, `runV1CutoverConformance`) reports each query's served answer against live, without the `today` column. No API enum changes; the dry run's `cutoverPath` is unchanged.

## [0.13.0] — The v1 cutover is on by default: v1 `#@ persist` and `#@ preaggregate` tables are served by the served copy and the rollup leg

`PUBLISHER_V1_SERVED_COPY` now defaults to `on` (materialization v2's v1 cutover, step 6f). This is the visible change of the cutover: v1 `#@ persist` tables, `storage=` and colocated, are answered by the served copy (the author's own files with each stored source re-rooted on its table), and v1 `#@ preaggregate` rollups by the rollup leg, instead of the storage serve shape, the `#@ preaggregate` composite and Malloy's build manifest on the live compile. Every answer read from a table equals the live answer in rows; what changes:

- **The path report** names the served copy (`servedBy.via: "served_copy"`) for a stored v1 source, and colocated tables are now listed as answering.
- **More shapes are answered from their table**: renames, imports under another name, a query-shaped source over an import, a named query, a nest, a keyed `join_one … with`, same-named sources in two models, an access-filtered extension of a stored source, a warehouse source joining a colocated one, an `extend` block that drops and re-hides stored columns, and a model file without `##! experimental.persistence` (planned from a build copy that carries the flag; every address unchanged). A stored `storage=` answer now carries its timeframes and its output columns' annotations (`# percent`, `#(doc)`, `# label`), which the serve shape dropped.
- **v1 rollups rebuild once.** A `#@ preaggregate` line is planned, built and served as a `#(preaggregate)` rollup, under the v2 table name (`<base>__rollup__<grain>__<hash>`, declared in its base's model only), so each rollup is built again once. Old `__preagg__` tables are left to the existing manifest reclaim. A rollup over a gated base, over rows that read a given, or over a `storage=` base follows the rollup leg's rules (warned and served live; built over the stored base); a colocated rollup over a gated base is built and read past its gates when `PUBLISHER_MATERIALIZE_GATED_SOURCES` is on and every gate reads a grain dimension. A gated base's rollup is no longer listed in the build plan's `refusedSources`: its `preaggregate-access-filter` warning is its only record. A query a rollup does not cover answers live with the source's own notes.
- **Answered live, never wrong**: a gate inherited through a query-shaped derivation that the derivation's re-root replaces (the served copy cannot keep it, so it declines rather than serve unfiltered rows); a stored column an `except:` hides whose stored name differs in case from the author's spelling (an upper-folding warehouse). A number's integer or decimal subtype is not carried on a colocated answer (known limitation 12). A stored column the served copy cannot declare (an undeclarable type, a nest a destination did not store, a big integer no cast reads exactly) is left out of its source, so a query reading it, by name or through a wildcard such as `select: *`, answers live while the rest of the source keeps its table.
- **Gated tables need one switch.** `PUBLISHER_MATERIALIZE_GATED_SOURCES` now applies under the cutover alone; `PUBLISHER_MATERIALIZE` is no longer needed with it.

Fixed on the way, on paths the cutover makes default: the served copy shares one compiled query model across queries rather than building one per query; a package whose only tables are colocated rollups routes to them after a manifest bind (the rollup leg had no context until a binding changed); the rollup leg answers a query through a model that imports the base without exporting it (#6646), and through an `index.malloy` that re-exports several sources; `#(preaggregate)` is not read under the cutover alone while `PUBLISHER_MATERIALIZE` is off; a v1 hidden-field finding is no longer reported twice; and the live compile reads no table at all, so a colocated table past its freshness window (`fallback: live`) is no longer read through the manifest a build reloads the models with.

`PUBLISHER_V1_SERVED_COPY=off` restores the old paths for one release, and `shadow` still compares them; both go with the retirement (6g). No API enum is added. Publisher does not authenticate callers: a gate holds only behind the gateway that sets the givens from a verified identity.

## [0.13.0] — In development: `PUBLISHER_V1_SERVED_COPY`, the v1 cutover's switch (off, shadow, on)

Introduced off by default (6a to 6e); the section above turns it on (6f). Materialization v2's v1 cutover: v1 `#@ persist` and `#@ preaggregate` tables are served by the served copy and the rollup and persisted-view legs instead of today's storage serve shape, `#@ preaggregate` composite and Malloy's build manifest on the live compile. `on`: a colocated `#@ persist` table is bound on the served copy with the columns its build captured (or, for a table built before, the persisted query's own output), read past a row-level gate with the gate grafted and proven, since it never leaves the author's warehouse (a gated v1 `#@ persist storage=` source stays live even with `PUBLISHER_MATERIALIZE_GATED_SOURCES` on: it is refused at build, reason `authorize`, so it has no table); its hidden columns, and those its `extend` block drops or renames, are kept for the author's own text to drop and hide again; a column an older build typed is cast on read, or left out so only a query reading it answers live; a `#@ preaggregate` rollup is the rollup leg's, `storage=` included, under the v2 rollup's table name, so it rebuilds once and answers with its measures' annotations; and a model file needs no `##! experimental.persistence` for its `#@ persist` sources to be planned (a build copy carries it, with every address unchanged). `shadow`: served as `off`, and each query a retiring path answered is answered again as `on` would, off the request path, at most two at once per server within a 30-second budget, recording no metric of the caller's query; the outcome is counted in `publisher_v1_served_copy_shadow_total` and a difference logged by place, never by value. A dry run (`POST …/packages?dryRun=true`) with the switch past `off` adds `cutoverPath` and `cutoverReason` (open strings) to each serve verdict, the path that will serve the source after the cutover. `scripts/v1-cutover-conformance.ts` runs the cutover's conformance check over a package snapshot. Behind `PUBLISHER_MATERIALIZE`, separately: a `#(materialize)` source over a base in its own file that declares measures, views or joins is now served (it kept the base's blocks). No enum is added. Publisher does not authenticate callers: a gate holds only behind the gateway that sets the givens from a verified identity.

## [0.13.0] — Malloy 0.0.438: a joined source with no matching row counts as none, and join-to-rollup serves counts

Publisher now builds on `@malloydata/*` 0.0.438, up from 0.0.436. The changes that reach a running server:

- **An aggregate at a joined source skips the rows where that source is unmatched** ([malloydata/malloy#3208](https://github.com/malloydata/malloy/pull/3208), fixing [#1762](https://github.com/malloydata/malloy/issues/1762)). A wrong answer is fixed in every package. Through a `join_many`, a parent with no joined row was counted as one child (`segments.count()` gave 1 for a flight with no segments), and a `sum` or `avg` of a value that is not NULL on that row (a constant, `??`, a column of the parent) read it once. Now `count()` counts the joined source's key, and a `sum` or `avg` skips the rows where it is NULL, so those queries return different, correct numbers. A ratio such as `miles.sum() / count()` over a parent with no rows is now 0 divided by 0, which DuckDB answers as NaN and Postgres refuses: a query grouped so that some group holds only parents with no joined rows (`run: flights -> { group_by: carrier; aggregate: segments.miles_per_seg }` with a carrier whose flights have no segments) now fails on Postgres with `division by zero`, where 0.0.436 answered 0. Guard such a ratio in the model (`miles.sum() / nullif(count(), 0)`). A `min` or `max` is not changed.
- **`!~` with a filter expression excludes the rows it matches** ([malloydata/malloy#3191](https://github.com/malloydata/malloy/pull/3191)). `x !~ f'abc'` used to return the same rows as `x ~ f'abc'`; it now returns the others, and a NULL passes unless the filter matches NULL. Existing `!~ f'…'` queries return different rows.
- **Drill-through reaches two more cells** ([malloydata/malloy#3204](https://github.com/malloydata/malloy/pull/3204), [malloydata/malloy#3158](https://github.com/malloydata/malloy/pull/3158)). A `drill:` on a null value (`drill: by_status.status is null`) is a drill clause instead of a compile error, so a report's or chart's null cell can be drilled; and a drill on a view grouped by a joined field (`group_by: customers.name`) joins it instead of failing with a missing-table error.
- **Postgres keeps `NUMERIC` precision in a sum through a join** ([malloydata/malloy#3144](https://github.com/malloydata/malloy/pull/3144)); **a renamed column below a filtered join** reads its own column again ([malloydata/malloy#3175](https://github.com/malloydata/malloy/pull/3175)); and **a line chart with several `# y` fields** drops only the null series' point, not the whole row ([malloydata/malloy#3196](https://github.com/malloydata/malloy/pull/3196)).

Behind `PUBLISHER_MATERIALIZE` (off by default), join-to-rollup now serves what #3208 made agree with live (materialization v2 known limitation 25, narrowed): a `count()` through a `join_many` (`flights -> { group_by: carrier; aggregate: segments.seg_count }`), a ratio over one, a sum whose value is not NULL on a parent with no rows, a join-level count, and a `count()`, `sum` or `avg` through another `join_many` beside a re-pointed join. Each was answered live (`COUNT_SEMANTICS`) and is now answered from the rollup, equal to live. Two shapes still read an unmatched parent's row live, and stay answered live (`COUNT_SEMANTICS`): a `min` or `max` of a value that is not NULL there (`max(coalesce(miles, 0))`), which Malloy does not skip, and an aggregate at a join of the joined source keyed on a computed dimension, which matches a row for that parent. A count, sum or average through such a join is served only when each build of the rollup found the joined source's own primary key unique and never NULL, where the join reaches it on another column (`on segments.flight_id = id`, with `primary_key: seg_id`). Since 0.0.438 live skips a row whose key is NULL there, and the rollup does not, so without that check a sum through the join, served before this release, would now differ from live. A repeated or NULL key, or no check on record (a table a control plane's manifest binds, say), is answered live (`COUNT_SEMANTICS`). The check runs for rollups in a `storage=` destination too, on the joined source's own connection.

Behind `PUBLISHER_MATERIALIZE`, **a pair table answers fewer counts from storage.** A pair table (`inline=` on a `join_many`) keeps one null-extended row for a parent with no child, which live used to count as that parent's one child; since #3208 live counts it as none, and the pair table cannot tell that row apart. A `count()` through the inlined join, at its last join or at a flagged middle level (`segments.count()`, a measure such as `seg_n is segments.count()`, a view that reads one), and a `sum` or `avg` there of a value that is not a stored column, are now answered live (`COUNT_SEMANTICS`), equal to live; sums, averages, `min`, `max` and distinct counts of stored columns are still served (materialization v2 known limitation 40). Without this, those queries would have been served wrong after the upgrade.

**Known regression in Malloy 0.0.438, live:** a sum through a nested repeated record of a query source whose parent key can be NULL drops that parent's nested rows. For example, with `source: nested is orders -> { group_by: region; nest: by_status is { group_by: status; aggregate: n is count() } }`, `run: nested -> { group_by: by_status.status; aggregate: n is by_status.n.sum() }` leaves out the orders whose `region` is NULL. #3208's unmatched-row test reads the unnested record's key, which is built from the parent's key and is NULL there. A stored (persisted or materialized) copy of such a source answers correctly, so it disagrees with live (materialization v2 known limitation 41, [malloydata/malloy#3220](https://github.com/malloydata/malloy/issues/3220)).

When a rollup's build SQL changes with Malloy's (a symmetric sum now reads `CASE WHEN key IS NOT NULL`), its content address changes, so such tables are rebuilt on the next run after the upgrade. The `@malloydata/render` tooltip patch is carried forward to 0.0.438, regenerated against its bundle. No API change. See docs/preaggregation.md, "Through a join", and docs/materialization.md, "The served copy".

## [0.13.0] — A cancelled run keeps the error it raced, and a failed shared table is built once

- A materialization run that was cancelled while a real failure was in flight still records `error:
"Cancelled"`, and now also keeps that failure's message in its metadata as `errorAtCancel`, on the
  record only; the logs carry its code.
- When a base and its `extend` share one table and its build fails, the second source takes the
  same failure (reason and `retryable`) without running the build again. The run's `failures` keep
  one entry per table, as before.

## [0.13.0] — The build plan says when it is incomplete: `omittedSources`

A build plan (`GET …/packages/{pkg}/build-plan`, the dry run, and the deprecated `Package.buildPlan`) now carries `omittedSources`, a list of `{ sourceID, reason }`: each source the plan would have held but left out because planning it failed, where before such a source vanished from the plan with only a log line. Failures it reports: a generated companion (the `#@ preaggregate` composite, the `#(preaggregate)` rollup companion, `#(materialize)`, persisted views, the v1 cutover's build copy) that did not compile, a `#@` annotation none of whose lines parse, and a source whose plan entry could not be projected. A companion whose planner failed before it could name its sources is listed in a second field, `omittedFiles` (`{ file, reason }`): retire nothing declared in that file. `reason` is an open string, a code such as `rollup_companion_failed`, never the failure's message. Both empty means every source the package plans is in `sources` or `refusedSources`, so a host can retire a table whose source is absent from both; otherwise keep the tables the entries name. A plan whose only sources were lost this way is now returned rather than read as no plan. A plan from an older Publisher has neither field; read that as completeness unknown. See [docs/materialization.md](docs/materialization.md#retiring-tables-the-plan-no-longer-lists). No enum is added.

Under the v1 cutover, two ways a model file without `##! experimental.persistence` lost its `#@ persist` sources are fixed: a `#@` line naming `persist` after another key (`#@ name=t persist`) is planned, as Malloy plans it in a flagged file, and a file that joins sources across connections is planned from its build view rather than from the file on disk, which never compiled.

## [0.13.0] — Materialization logs no longer carry watermark values or driver messages

A materialization log line no longer carries a value from the data or a driver's error message, which
can quote the build's SQL or a row value. The detail is still on the run's record. Log pipelines that
read these fields should switch to the codes:

- "Rebuilding an incremental source in full" and "Skipping an incremental source's refresh" drop
  `reason` (it could name a watermark boundary) and keep `reasonCode`. "Applied an incremental delta"
  drops `rangeStart` and `rangeEnd`. The boundary reached is on the manifest entry's `ledger`.
- "Could not read a covered_through boundary after a full rebuild" carries `errorCode`, not `error`.
- "Chained storage build could not reuse the parent table" carries `code` (a driver's code,
  Publisher's error kind or the error's class), not `reason`; the cast fallback and the two rollback
  warnings carry `errorCode` or `causeCode`.
- "Materialization run failed" and "Materialization run cancelled", logged for a run failure that
  `materialization.run.finished` did not already report, carry `code` and, for a failure, the
  stack's frames without its message line.

## [0.13.0] — (BREAKING) Materialization build metrics: one build counter, and structured run and build events

Three materialization metrics are replaced, and one loses a label. Dashboards or alerts on the old
names stop receiving data.

- `publisher_materialization_sources_total{outcome, mode}` and
  `publisher_storage_build_failures_total{destination, reason}` fold into
  `publisher_materialization_build_total{kind, tier, outcome, failure_class}`, counted once per
  source per run. `kind` is `materialize`, `persist`, `rollup`, `view` or `pair`; `tier` is
  `colocated` or `storage`; `outcome` is `built`, `reused`, `refused`, `failed` or `cancelled`; and
  `failure_class` is `none` unless the build failed, then `deterministic`, `transient`,
  `unclassified` (the per-source `retryable` false, true and absent) or `billed_read_lost` (the old
  `reason="billed_read_not_captured"`: the warehouse read was charged and its rows were lost, so a
  retry pays again). Colocated failures are now counted too, not only `storage=` ones. The run's
  `mode` stays on `publisher_materialization_runs_total`. A failed build is counted even when the
  whole run then fails, where the old counter counted nothing for such a run; a reused source is
  counted only when its run commits.
- `publisher_materialization_source_build_duration_ms{engine}` becomes
  `publisher_materialization_build_duration_ms{kind, tier, method}`, with explicit buckets from
  100 ms to an hour. The old `engine` maps as `in_warehouse` to colocated/full, `storage` to
  storage/full, `delta` to colocated/delta and `delta_storage` to storage/delta. A failed build that
  started is timed too.
- New: `publisher_materialization_build_read_bytes{tier}`, the warehouse bytes a build scanned,
  recorded only when the warehouse reported a count.
- `publisher_storage_tables_retained_total` drops its `destination` label; the destination is on
  the warn log beside each count.

The run's log lines change with them. `materialization.run.started` (info) and
`materialization.run.finished` (info, warn when partial, error when failed) replace "Materialization
build started" and "Materialization build complete…", and `materialization.build.finished` (info) and
`materialization.build.failed` (warn, error when unclassified) replace "Source failed to
materialize". Each carries `runId` (the run's id), the source's `sourceEntityId`, `kind`, `tier`,
`method` and, for a failure, `failureClass` and `code`. A failure's message is no longer logged, since
a driver error can quote SQL or a value: it stays on the run's record (`error`, and each
`failures[].reason`), and the log carries its code. A whole-run failure is logged once, by
`materialization.run.finished`, rather than again as "Materialization run failed".

## [0.13.0] — In development: integers past 2^53 served from storage come back exact

A wrong answer is fixed. A query answered from a stored table (`storage=`, colocated
`#(materialize)`, a v1 colocated table under `PUBLISHER_V1_SERVED_COPY=on`, and the storage serve
shape) read a big-integer column through the table's plain
`number` declaration, so a value above 2^53 came back rounded: 9007199254740993 as
9007199254740992, where live on DuckDB, BigQuery or Snowflake gives every digit (materialization v2
known limitation 12, which said answers were equal and only metadata differed).

A column whose field Malloy types as a big integer (`BIGINT`, `HUGEINT`, `UBIGINT`, `INT64`,
`NUMBER(p,0)`, a sum or max over one) is now read through a native cast, so it stays served from
storage and comes back exact, with live's `bigint` subtype. In a `storage=` table the cast is
`::"HUGEINT"`. In a colocated one it is the column's own warehouse type, which each colocated build
now reads from the warehouse's catalog, so no value is narrowed (a DuckDB `UHUGEINT` past
2^127 − 1, SQL Server's `decimal(38,0)`). Selecting, grouping, filtering and aggregating it, a
`primary_key:` and the author's own measures over it all keep serving. A column no cast reads
exactly is left out per query and answered live: one stored as a float, a colocated column whose
warehouse type Malloy does not read as a big integer (Postgres stores a sum of `BIGINT`s as
`numeric`; a MySQL integer, which MySQL's `CAST` cannot name), and a colocated column whose build did
not record its type (a table built before this release, or an unqualified name the warehouse's
`information_schema` finds in more than one schema). On Postgres, whose live answer itself rounds such values (its rows come back through
JSON), served equals live, never more precise. `count()`, 32-bit integers and decimals are
unchanged.

API: a build manifest entry gains `nativeSchema`, each colocated column with its warehouse type,
recorded by every colocated build and incremental refresh. A host that stores and replays manifests
should keep it; without it, a colocated table's big-integer columns are answered live. See
docs/materialization.md, "Stored column types follow the model, not the warehouse".

## [0.13.0] — A colocated `#@ persist` table past its freshness window is no longer read

A wrong answer is fixed, with the default settings as well as under the v1 cutover. After a host binds a build manifest, a query on a `#@ persist` source whose colocated table was past its freshness window (`freshness.fallback` `live` or `fail`) could still read that table, while the path report said `servedBy: live`. With the default `PUBLISHER_V1_SERVED_COPY=off` this happened when the stale table's only fresh neighbours were `#@ preaggregate` rollups or persisted views; under `on` it happened to every such table, and `shadow` compared against that answer. Such a query is now answered live, as its fallback says.

## [0.13.0] — A `.malloynb` cell over a model without the persistence flag runs beside a bound table

A legacy `.malloynb` notebook cell failed with "A non-empty `buildManifest` was supplied, but the model is missing `##! experimental.persistence`" whenever its package had a colocated `#@ persist` table bound and the cell's model did not import a model that carries the flag. A cell now gets the bound tables only when its own model carries the flag, as a query on a model already did.

## [0.13.0] — `/compile`'s SQL preview no longer names a table past its freshness window

With `includeSql`, `POST …/models/{path}/compile` and the `compile_model` MCP tool previewed SQL against every bound colocated table, including one past its freshness window that execution no longer reads. The preview now uses the same freshness-filtered manifest as execution, so its SQL reads the base table where the query would. A table within its window is still previewed.

## [0.13.0] — In development: join-to-rollup checks the querying source's primary key, and counts beside a re-pointed join as live does

Behind `PUBLISHER_MATERIALIZE` (off by default). Two wrong answers from a joined source's `#(preaggregate)` rollup read through a join are fixed, and each now equals live.

- **A declared `primary_key` the data breaks.** A join read as a `join_many` (`flights` with `primary_key: id` and `join_many: segments on segments.flight_id = id`) was served on the declared key alone. With `id` repeated, a rollup row was read once per row sharing it (10 against live's 5); with an `id` NULL, the variant counted a row live skips (6 against 5). Each build of the rollup now also checks every source in the package that reads it through such a join, grouping that source's rows on its primary key, and records whether a value repeats or is NULL, in the same run record as the `join_one` key check, carried and forgotten with the rollup's table the same way. Unique and never NULL is served; repeated, NULL, or not on record (a table a control plane's manifest binds, a check that could not run) answers live. A repeat or NULL is logged at build. Through a rollup in a `storage=` destination, read beside the querying source's stored table there, the stored table's own build checks the key over the rows it holds, under the same rules. A querying source whose `where:` reads a given, with or without a default, is not checked through a colocated rollup, since a check compiled once would read the given's default rows rather than each caller's, and is answered live.
- **A count through another `join_many` beside a re-pointed join.** Reading `segments` at its key as a `join_one` hid its fan-out from Malloy, which then wrote another `join_many`'s `count()` as `COUNT(1)` and counted a flight with no certs as one cert (6 against live's 4). Malloy 0.0.438 (malloydata/malloy#3208, in this release) counts that flight as no certs whichever way it writes the count, so such a query is served from the rollup and equals live.

## [0.13.0] — In development: a pair table's middle sums beside the leaf, and incremental refresh for paths and blocks

Behind `PUBLISHER_MATERIALIZE` (off by default). Two pair-table gaps close (materialization v2 known limitation 9):

- **A middle level beside the leaf.** In a path of join_manys (`inline=["items.options"]`), a sum or an average of a stored column of `items` (`items.price.sum()` declared on the source) beside `items.options` fields was answered live; it is now answered from the table when every join down to `items` is keyed on the level above's primary key (`join_many: items on items.order_id = id`), which the build already checks unique and never null, so each item has one order. A middle count, an aggregate of a computed middle field, and a level joined on anything else stay live.
- **Incremental paths and blocks.** A path's pair table, and a table of several inlined join_manys, declared `refresh="incremental"` used to rebuild in full (`materialize-pair-full-refresh`). They now refresh in place as a one-join pair table does, replacing whole parents, when the watermark names a field of the source and of every level of every path (`watermark=["updated_at", "items.loaded_at", "items.options.loaded_at"]`). Each refresh checks every level's row flag, and for blocks every block's flags and that each parent keeps rows in every block, and rolls back to a full rebuild if one fails. A table of several blocks stores one more internal column, `__pair_watermark_block`. A watermark missing a level still rebuilds in full, with the warning naming the level.

No API change. See docs/materialization.md, "An incremental pair table".

## [0.13.0] — In development: a `#(preaggregate)` rollup no query reads, over a source with its own time zone, is not built

Behind `PUBLISHER_MATERIALIZE` (off by default). A query on a source that sets its own `timezone:` is never answered from a rollup (`TIME_ZONE`), yet the rollup was still planned and built. Now such a rollup, on a source that sets or inherits its own `timezone:`, is not built, with a `preaggregate-time-zone` warning, unless another source in the same zone joins it, which a query on that source still reads through the join (colocated, or in a `storage=` destination that source is stored in too). Answers are unchanged; the build no query read is gone. No API change. See docs/preaggregation.md.

## [0.13.0] — In development: a `#(materialize)` source over a table-backed base scoped by a given builds through a rename, its own `where:` or a join

Behind `PUBLISHER_MATERIALIZE` (off by default). Over a base that reads a table (`duckdb.table('orders')`) and keeps one tenant's rows, a `#(materialize)` extension reached through a rename (`source: b2 is base`), or one that adds its own `where:` or join (or sits below a source that does), was refused (`materialize-not-built`) and answered live, though the same shapes built over a SQL base. Now each is built with every caller's rows and served per caller from its table, as over a SQL base. No API change. See docs/materialization.md, "A base scoped by a given".

## [0.13.0] — In development: a joined source's `storage=` rollup is read through the join when the querying source is stored in the same destination

Behind `PUBLISHER_MATERIALIZE` and the storage tier (`PERSIST_STORAGE_MODE=on`). A query that reads a joined source's measures through a join (`run: flights -> { group_by: carrier; aggregate: segments.seg_miles }`) used to skip that source's `#(preaggregate)` rollup whenever the rollup was in a `storage=` destination (`CROSS_CONNECTION`), because the querying source read its own connection and Malloy joins within one. Now, when the querying source is itself stored in that destination (a `#(materialize) storage=` table, or a `#@ persist storage=` source), the query is answered there: the querying source is read as the served copy declares it, over its stored table, and the join is re-pointed at the rollup, so both tables are read on the destination in one query. Every answer equals live, including parents with no joined rows and NULL measures; the querying source's given-reading `where:` terms and rolling windows are applied at read as the served copy applies them; hidden fields stay hidden. Both tables must be fresh. Still answered without the rollup: a querying source not stored in that destination, or whose table there is not built or not fresh, or a reader that opts out with `#@ -persist` (`CROSS_CONNECTION`); a definition of the querying source that the served copy leaves out because it reads the join to a source not stored there, such as a measure or view over `segments` (`CROSS_CONNECTION`); a querying source stored as a pair table, and the served copy's rules for a join it stores inline (`COUNT_SEMANTICS`, `MISSING_FIELD`); and every decline the join leg already had (a gated entry point stays `CONTRACT`, with `PUBLISHER_MATERIALIZE_GATED_SOURCES` on as well). A failed run is retried live only when every table it read allows it. No API enum changes. See docs/preaggregation.md, "Through a join".

## [0.13.0] — In development: one source's served-copy failure no longer sends its whole model live

Behind `PUBLISHER_MATERIALIZE` (off by default). The served copy is compiled once per model, so a stored source whose re-root did not compile used to fail the whole copy, and every stored source in that model answered live (correct answers, but every table in the model went unused). Now the failure is traced to the re-root it is in, and that source alone steps back: a source that inlines join_ones keeps them as written first, an extension table falls back to its own blocks, and otherwise the source answers live with a `served-copy-not-served` warning (`reroot_not_compiled`). The rest of the model compiles again and keeps its tables. A failure outside every re-root is handled as before.

Two shapes that hit this now work. A `#(materialize)` source whose rolling-window `where:` reads an `internal` or `private` dimension it defines (`internal dimension: t2 is ts; where: t2 >= now - 60 days`), with a lower, upper or two-sided bound, failed with `'t2' is not defined`. The window is now applied by the source's own text, as you wrote it, and confirmed in the served source's compiled filters, so it is answered from the stored table and matches live at every clock. A pair table (an inlined join_many) beside a column kept hidden under its own name (an `include { private: … }`) is now answered from its table too: its stored columns are renamed ahead of that `include`, since Malloy refuses a `rename:` right after one. The hidden columns stay exactly as hidden as live keeps them on every caller path. A pair source refused for an author `rename:` behind such an `include` is now reported as `definition_not_parsed` rather than `pair_join_not_found`.

## [0.13.0] — In development: a one-hop pair table over a null or repeated primary key is not built

Behind `PUBLISHER_MATERIALIZE` (off by default). A one-hop pair table (`inline=["segs"]` on a single join_many) marks one `__parent_row` per distinct primary key, so two parents with a null key, or two with the same key, shared one flagged row, and the served copy answered parent measures beside the join wrong (`flight_count` 1 against live's 0 for two null-keyed flights, `total_distance` 30 against 70 for one key held twice). Each build of a one-hop pair table, full or incremental, now first checks that the source's primary key is unique and never null, as path and block tables already did, and is refused otherwise, so the source answers live. The check reads the rows the build stores, so a term the build leaves out (a given's, a rolling window's upper bound) is left out of the check too, and a key held by two tenants, or repeated past the window's cut-off, refuses the build. The check costs one `GROUP BY` of the source on its primary key per build. No API field changes.

## [0.13.0] — In development: a `#(materialize)` build failure costs one source, not the model

Behind `PUBLISHER_MATERIALIZE` (off by default). Found in the review of #1678. A source whose generated build text does not compile is now refused on its own (`materialize-not-built`, "its generated build did not compile", a Publisher bug worth reporting) and answers live, and the rest of the model builds; before, the whole generated build file failed and no `#(materialize)` source in the model was built. An extension table whose build does not compile over its parent's table builds over the chain from the warehouse (same rows) alone; the model's other extensions keep building over their parents' tables, where before one failure sent all of them to the warehouse. No API enum changes. See docs/materialization.md, "Extension tables" and the `inline=` entries.

## [0.13.0] — In development: `inline=` takes a hidden join_many

Behind `PUBLISHER_MATERIALIZE` (off by default). `inline=` may now name an `internal` or `private` join_many, which was refused (`materialize-not-built`) and served live. Its pair table is built, and the served copy declares the join's record under your modifier, with the stored columns behind it `private`. So a caller reads `j.<field>` exactly where live lets it: an `internal` join through the caller's own `extend`, a `private` one never, and the stored `j__<field>` columns never. Your own dimensions, measures, views and gates over the join are answered from the table with live's rows. This holds for a path of join_manys (each level's columns are `private` under a hidden first join) and for each block of a table that inlines several. A path through a join that the joined source itself hides (`inline=["items.options"]` where `items` declares `internal join_many: options`) is refused for that source alone with a reason. Before, it stopped the build of every `#(materialize)` source in the model. A colocated `#(materialize)` extension of a source that inlines a join_many, public or hidden, is now built over the chain from the warehouse: it was built over the parent's pair table, which holds each parent once per child, and answered its parent measures and the join's measures too high. See [the served copy](docs/materialization.md#the-served-copy-in-development-publisher_materialize).

## [0.13.0] — In development: a joined source's rollup answers a query that also aggregates through a join_one, once its key is checked unique

Materialization v2 known limitation 29 lifted, behind `PUBLISHER_MATERIALIZE` (off by default).

Join-to-rollup used to answer live any query through a `join_one` that also aggregated the querying source's own rows (`flight_count` beside `crew.crew_size`), because a `join_one` the data does not keep unique repeats parent rows live. Now a `#(preaggregate)` rollup whose one grain dimension is a `join_one`'s key gets a uniqueness check on every auto-run build, over the rows the build read: when no key value repeats, those queries are served from the rollup; when one repeats, they stay live, the build logs that the declared `join_one` is broken, and the package carries a `preaggregate-join-one-key-repeated` warning on the rollup's source until a build finds the key unique. A query that reads another `join_one` whose key a build found repeated is answered live too, closing a case where served and live could differ (15.5 live against 10.5 served). With no check on record, as for a table a control plane's manifest binds, behaviour is as before. The check is recorded beside the inline uniqueness check in `metadata.inlineUniquenessChecks.rollupKeys`, describes only the table its run wrote, is carried while that table stands, and is restored on restart. Rollups no `join_one` reads are not checked. No API field changes. See [docs/preaggregation.md](docs/preaggregation.md).

## [0.13.0] — In development: join-to-rollup reads fan-out grains and join-level measures, and refinement views route to rollups

Behind `PUBLISHER_MATERIALIZE` (off by default), two `#(preaggregate)` rollup gaps close ([docs/preaggregation.md](docs/preaggregation.md)). Through a join, a joined source's rollup with a fan-out grain dimension or a join-level sum or count is now read under the same rule as the source's own queries: `run: flights -> { group_by: segments.line_kind; aggregate: segments.seg_miles }`, or the same with `where: segments.line_kind = 'a'`, is answered from the rollup, equal to live, at every nest level that groups or fixes the dimension; a join-level sum is answered when its other grain dimensions are grouped or fixed, and grouping by the querying source's join key (`group_by: id`) fixes the join's. A query that drops the dimension, fixes it to two values or in one branch of an `or`, or reads the measure where the dimension is not fixed is answered live (`GRAIN_TOO_COARSE`). A join-level measure's column (`kinds.weight.max()`) is now read through a join when its join is keyed on a column, where it used to be answered live; one keyed on a computed dimension stays live (`COUNT_SEMANTICS`). And a view defined as a refinement of another (`view: a is b + { … }`, at any depth) routes to a rollup like any named view; a refinement whose text or base changed on disk since the model compiled is answered live. No API enum changes. With the switch off nothing changes.

## [0.13.0] — Persisted tables are named for their package, so packages sharing a schema no longer serve each other's rows

Auto-run (Publisher's own builds) used to name a persisted table after its source, or its `name=`. Two packages, or two environments, whose models point at the same warehouse schema or storage destination and persist a source of the same name wrote the **same** table: each build overwrote the other's rows, and every package served whichever built last. Nothing reported it: wrong answers, and possibly one tenant's rows served to another.

- **Default names now carry the package.** A table whose name the author did not choose (a `#@ persist` source with no `name=`, a `#(materialize) storage=` source with no `name=`, a rollup) is named `<source>__p<8 hex>`, the hex a hash of the environment and package, so no two packages on one server share it. `scope: version` tables keep their version suffix (`__v1_2_0_<hex>`), which already hashed both.
- **An explicit `name=` keeps its name** and is checked before every build. The table is marked with a comment, `malloy-publisher:table owner=<environment>/<package>`. A `name=` held by a table another package marked, another package's view, or anything Publisher did not make, is refused for that source, coded `table-owned-elsewhere` in the run's failures, before anything is written, and the source answers live. A holder Publisher cannot read is refused too (`table-ownership-unverified`), and so is a `name=` spelled like one of Publisher's own package or version names (ending `__p<8 hex>` or `__v<version>_<8 hex>`). Two packages building one `name=` at once on one server take turns, so one builds it and the other is refused. A package's entries retired for a table held elsewhere, or replaced by its `name=` view, never again count as its record of that table. Give one of the sources another `name=`.
- **Deleting a run with `dropTables=true` never drops a table another package has marked since.**
- **Upgrading rebuilds, it never deletes.** The first auto-run after the upgrade rebuilds each default-named source under its new name (a one-time rebuild per package); the old table is left where it is, named by the old runs, and dropped when those runs are deleted with `dropTables=true`. Until that first build a package serves its old tables as before, so build each package once after upgrading. An existing `name=` table without a mark is claimed by the first package whose own records name it, and marked; any other package whose records also name it is then refused it and answers live.
- A `#(materialize)` source with no `name=` no longer gets a `name=` view at its source's name: that name was Publisher's default, not the author's (behind `PUBLISHER_MATERIALIZE`).

Host-orchestrated builds are unchanged: the host chooses those names. The hash keeps tables apart within one server; two servers whose environments and packages have the same names must still not share a schema. See [docs/materialization.md](docs/materialization.md#whose-table-it-is).

## [0.13.0] — In development: `#(materialize)` stores an "older than" rolling window

Behind `PUBLISHER_MATERIALIZE` (off by default). A `#(materialize)` source whose `where:` keeps rows older than a moving cut-off (`ts < now - 30 days`) used to be left unbuilt (`materialize-not-built`) and served live, because the table would have had to be built as of the end of a refresh interval Publisher does not know. Now the term is left out of the build, so the table holds every row there is when it is built, and the served copy re-applies it at every read, whether the source writes it or inherits it from a base in the same file. No scheduler or refresh interval is needed. A two-sided window (`ts >= now - 60 days and ts < now - 30 days`, the same written as two `where:` terms, or the range `ts ? now - 60 days to now - 30 days`) builds its lower bound and leaves its upper bound out; an incremental refresh deletes below the lower bound only, and an upper bound alone deletes nothing. The build writes no clock value, so the table's address does not move between builds. An upper bound written in another file than the source's model, an inherited one that a join named in `inline=` also applies, any other `where:` that reads `now`, and a query that sets a `timezone:` still answer live. See docs/materialization.md, "Rolling windows".

## [0.13.0] — In development: a gated query is answered from a colocated `#(preaggregate)` rollup, the gate proven on it

Behind `PUBLISHER_MATERIALIZE` and `PUBLISHER_MATERIALIZE_GATED_SOURCES` (both off by default). A query whose entry point carries a row-level gate (`#(access_filter)`) or a lock (`#(authorize)`) used to skip every rollup (`CONTRACT`), so governed models got no rollup speedup. Now it is answered from a colocated `#(preaggregate)` rollup over its source when every field the gate reads is one of the rollup's grain dimensions (a column, a dimension computed from the source's own columns, or a truncation); a lock that reads no field, a lock beside a filter, an inherited gate, and `#(authorize) true` re-opening a locked base beside a filter count as their parts. The queried source is redeclared over the rollup in its own file with its gates, keeping its identity, and the gate is grafted and proven there as on live, so each caller gets live's answer over the rows its gate admits; a rollup is used only when the gates written on it equal the live source's. An `internal` grain dimension a gate reads is the one hidden field a rollup stores, and stays `internal`. With the switch off, no rollup over a gated source is built (`preaggregate-access-filter`), as before. A gate field the grain drops, a gate through a join, a source that joins a gated source, a caller join into a gated source, a joined source's rollup under a gated parent, and a `storage=` rollup over a gated source (until the managed tier's security review) are answered live, a skipped rollup reporting `CONTRACT` with a detail that never names the gate. No API enum changes. Publisher does not authenticate callers: the gate holds only behind the gateway that sets the givens from a verified identity. See docs/preaggregation.md and docs/authorize.md.

## [0.13.0] — In development: a `#(materialize)` source over a base scoped by a given is built and served per caller

Behind `PUBLISHER_MATERIALIZE` (off by default). The common governed shape, a base that keeps one tenant's rows (`where: org_id = $ORG_ID`) or declares a dimension that reads a given, with `#(materialize)` extensions over it, used to leave each extension unbuilt and answered live: the base's term and dimension were refused. Now, when the base is one the source extends or renames in the same file, the base's term is left out of the build (the build reads a copy of the file with it written `true`) and so is the base's given-reading dimension, so the table holds every caller's rows and no caller's value; the served copy keeps that base's `extend` blocks over the stored table, so the term is applied and the dimension computed at read with each caller's value, as written. A time-zone-dependent dimension declared on such a base is computed at read too, so a `timezone:` query over its table is answered from it. A base in another file, a term in a parenthesised head, a source that renames, redefines, drops or re-hides a field of the base, or a join of the source that reads the base still leaves the source unbuilt, with a `materialize-not-built` warning that says why, and it serves live. A served copy whose compiled filters lost a given-reading term is still never read (`read_terms_not_kept`). No API change. See docs/materialization.md, "A base scoped by a given".

## [0.13.0] — In development: a colocated `#(materialize)` is built and served from its own warehouse

Behind `PUBLISHER_MATERIALIZE` (off by default). A `#(materialize)` source with no `storage=` is built into its own warehouse again (it needs a `name=` there, since its default table could be the one it reads, and a `name=` already holding a table no run of the package wrote, or a view Publisher did not make, fails that source's build before anything is written), and the served copy answers it from that table, read on the source's own connection exactly as a `storage=` table is read in its destination. Everything the served copy does for `storage=` applies: stored computed dimensions and timeframes, `inline=` joins and pair tables, private and internal fields, given and rolling-window terms re-applied at read, extension tables built over their parent's table, and row-level gates grafted and proven on the served compile. A source reached only through a join now reads its table too. It needs no storage tier (`PERSIST_STORAGE_MODE` decides only `storage=` tables), and a gated one is built and served only with `PUBLISHER_MATERIALIZE_GATED_SOURCES` on, as a `storage=` one is. An answer from colocated tables alone reports no `servedFrom`, as a colocated `#@ persist` answer does; its path report names the table, `via: "served_copy"`. The "colocated #(materialize) is not served yet" warning is gone. v1's colocated `#@ persist` is unchanged, served through Malloy's build manifest. No API field or enum changes. See [docs/materialization.md](docs/materialization.md).

## [0.13.0] — In development: a `#(materialize)` dimension that depends on the caller is computed at read

Behind `PUBLISHER_MATERIALIZE` (off by default). A `#(materialize)` source with a dimension that reads a given used to be refused whole (`given_in_persisted_query`) and answered live. Now just that dimension is left out of the build, and the served copy computes it at read from the stored columns, so each caller gets its own value and the rest of the source serves from its table (materialization v2, P9). The same holds for a dimension that reads the current time, as before, and, new, for one that depends on the query's time zone (`hour(ts)`, `ts.month`): a `timezone:` query over a table whose own stored dimensions are all zone-free is now answered from the table instead of live. A table whose rows a zone-dependent `where:` filtered (a timestamp literal) now declines `timezone:` queries; before, such a table with no stored computed dimension served them, and a zone ahead of UTC could miss rows the build left out. Publisher decides by compiling small probe queries against the model on the load worker (never running them), beside its reading of the compiled model. What still answers live, with a `materialize-not-built` warning: a given-reading dimension declared on a base in another file (one declared on a base in the same file is computed at read; see the entry above), and an `inline=` join through which a given is read. A zone-dependent dimension declared on a base in another file is stored as before and its table still declines `timezone:` queries. No API change. See docs/materialization.md, "Dimensions that depend on the caller".

## [0.13.0] — In development: pair tables for a path of join_manys and for more than one join_many

Behind `PUBLISHER_MATERIALIZE`. `#(materialize) inline=` now takes a path of join_manys (`inline=["items.options"]`), stored as one pair table with a row flag per level above the last join, and more than one join_many (`inline=["items", "payments"]`), stored as blocks of one table marked by a new `__pair_lane` column. A query is answered from the one block it reads; a query that reads two blocks, aggregates a middle level beside the last one, or aggregates a level above the last one in the query rather than through a measure, is answered live, as is any other shape the table cannot reproduce exactly. A path through a join_one is refused. Those tables rebuild in full when declared incremental (`materialize-pair-full-refresh`). Each build of such a table first checks that the source's primary key and every middle level's key are unique and never null, and is refused otherwise (a level's row flag counts one row per key), so the source answers live. Also fixed: a row-level gate through a join_many the pair table does not inline, at any step of its path (`hub.gates.gate` through a join_one), is now answered live, and so is a query that groups or filters through such a path; before, served child aggregates under either could be wrong.

## [0.13.0] — In development: an inlined join_many's pair table refreshes incrementally

Behind `PUBLISHER_MATERIALIZE` (off by default). A `#(materialize)` source that inlines a join_many (a pair table) and declares `refresh="incremental"` was refused and served live; it is now built and served, and refreshes in place when its watermark names a field on each side of the join: `watermark=["updated_at", "segments.loaded_at"]`. The table gains a `__pair_watermark` column, per parent the greatest of those fields over the parent and its children, and each refresh replaces every row of each parent whose watermark moved, by the parent's primary key, in one transaction in the destination that fails, and rolls back to a full rebuild, unless every parent keeps exactly one `__parent_row`. A late-arriving child of an old parent, a parent gaining or losing children with its own field moved, and new parents with or without children all reach the table, which equals a full rebuild after each refresh. A child deleted or moved to another parent reaches it only when the old parent's own field moves too, and a parent whose fields are all null, on its own row and every child's, only at a full build. The range a refresh reads is open above, so a child stamped later than the refresh's clock does not hold its parent's later changes back. A watermark that names only the source's own fields (a child added to a stored parent could not be seen), only the join's, an unstored field or fields of mixed types, a `merge_key=` other than the parent key, or a rolling window over a field of the join rebuilds the table in full on every refresh, with a `materialize-pair-full-refresh` warning; the table is still served. No API enum changes. See docs/materialization.md, "An incremental pair table".

## [0.13.0] — Security: a stored answer past a gate must enforce every gate live does

Behind `PUBLISHER_MATERIALIZE` and `PUBLISHER_MATERIALIZE_GATED_SOURCES` (both off by default). When a query whose entry point carries a gate is answered from a stored copy (the served copy of a `#(materialize)` source, or a persisted view), Publisher re-proves the gate on the stored answer's own compile before running it. That check passed as soon as it found any one gate enforced there, so a stored form that kept an `#(authorize)` lock but lost an `#(access_filter)`, or lost an inherited gate, would have answered rows the live query refuses. It now requires the gates enforced on the stored answer to be exactly the live entry point's, every `#(authorize)` and `#(access_filter)`, own and inherited, by route and expression. Any difference, or a live gate set it cannot read, denies the query with the usual opaque 403. The stored forms shipped today write every gate onto their compile, so a correctly built package answers as before. Gates hold only behind the authenticating gateway that sets the givens ([docs/security-posture.md](docs/security-posture.md#operating-model-a-microservice-behind-your-gateway)).

## [0.13.0] — In development: the inline uniqueness check skips an unchanged table, and `#(carries)` reads the served copy

Two materialization v2 limitations lifted, both behind `PUBLISHER_MATERIALIZE` (off by default).

The `inline=` join_one uniqueness check no longer runs on every auto-run build. It is skipped when its answer cannot have changed: the joined source is a `#@ persist` table the build reads, that table was not written since a check over it passed in the run before, every other run of the package had finished before that run began, and the check's SQL is the same. A joined warehouse or incremental table is still checked on every build, since its rows change under one address, and builds a control plane instructs always run it. When the build reads the joined source's stored table, the check now reads that table too. Each run records its checks in `metadata.inlineUniquenessChecks`; deleting a run's record forgets the passes the package's other runs record, so the next run checks again. No API field changes.

The per-request `#(carries)` ceiling check now reads the compile that answers. A query the served copy answers is checked on the served copy's compile, and on live too when live compiles. So a clean query through a join between sources on two connections, which a model loads live with that join left out, is now served once both sides are stored, where it used to be refused. A query reading a class past the ceiling is still refused, served or live, a served answer that falls back to live is checked against live, and anything the served copy's compile cannot show is refused. See [docs/materialization.md](docs/materialization.md) and [docs/classification.md](docs/classification.md#the-ceiling-is-checked-per-query).

## [0.13.0] — In development: `#(preaggregate)` rolls a measure up behind PUBLISHER_MATERIALIZE

With `PUBLISHER_MATERIALIZE` on (off by default), `#(preaggregate) grain=["category"]` on a measure stores it rolled up to that grain, and a query the rollup reproduces exactly is answered from it (materialization v2, phase 4; [docs/preaggregation.md](docs/preaggregation.md)). Measures qualify by their own text, checked against the compiled measure: sums, counts, mins and maxes, filtered or not, and expressions of them (`revenue / order_count`, `coalesce(x.max(), 0)`), each stored as partials and merged at read. A source with a `join_many` may now be rolled up: a grain dimension read through it must be grouped or fixed to one value by the query. A join-level sum or count (`carriers.fleet.sum()`, with the join's key in the grain) is read from the rollup only when every other grain dimension is grouped or fixed too. A query that supplies a given routes; a query that sets a `timezone:`, in any stage or nest, does not. A rollup over a `#@ persist storage=` base builds and serves (#6293), and a rollup is planned once, under the model that declares its base, however many models import it, so the build plan lists it once.

A malformed declaration (a measure whose partials cannot be merged, an unknown key, a grain naming no dimension) is refused at publish, and is a warning on load. One that cannot be honoured here is a coded warning and the measure serves live: a join-level aggregate whose key is not in the grain or that is taken through more than one join, an access filter on a field the grain drops or read through a join, a build that reads a given, a source, grain dimension or measure that reads the current time (a rolling window would be fixed at build time), or a measure Publisher cannot read with certainty. A gated entry point (`#(authorize)`, `#(access_filter)`) is never answered from a rollup. Whether a query routes is read from its compiled form, not its text. The path report says why a rollup did not answer a query (`GRAIN_TOO_COARSE`, `MISSING_FIELD`, `COUNT_SEMANTICS`, `TIME_ZONE`, `NOT_BUILT`, `CONTRACT`); no API enum changes. A rollup's answer returns each column with the annotations live's does (`#(classification)`, `#(doc)`, render tags such as `# currency`), from a source's own rollup and through a join alike, a multi-line `#|`…`|#` note included (one used to stop the rollup or served copy compiling, so the query was answered live); the access record's classes and the `#(carries)` ceiling read the live compile. With the switch off nothing changes, and `#@ preaggregate` keeps its v1 behaviour either way.

## [0.13.0] — In development: `#(preaggregate)` rollups answer named views, extensions, and join-level max and min, and are not built over a gated source

Behind `PUBLISHER_MATERIALIZE` (off by default), four gaps in the `#(preaggregate)` rollup leg close ([docs/preaggregation.md](docs/preaggregation.md)). A query that calls a named view (`run: orders -> by_category`, refined, continued or nested) is answered from a rollup when the view's own query is one the rollup reproduces; a persisted view of that name still answers first, and a view whose file was edited since the model compiled, or that reads raw SQL, is answered live. A query on an extension or rename of a rolled-up source is answered from that source's rollups when the extension adds no `where:`, gate or `timezone:` and binds no base field's name to another field, and the query reads only grain dimensions, stored measures and the extension's dimensions over grain dimensions. A join-level `max` or `min` (`carriers.fleet.max()`, its join's key in the grain) is stored and merged with `max` or `min`, `NULL` where live is `NULL`; it used to be answered live. And while a gated entry point is answered live (`CONTRACT`), a rollup over a gated source is no longer built, even when its grain keeps the gate's field: its declaration is a `preaggregate-access-filter` warning, so no warehouse time goes to a table nothing reads. No API enum changes. With the switch off nothing changes.

## [0.13.0] — In development: a joined source's `#(preaggregate)` rollup answers through the join

Behind `PUBLISHER_MATERIALIZE` (off by default). A query that reads a joined source's measures, `run: flights -> { group_by: carrier; aggregate: segments.seg_miles }`, is now answered from `segments`' `#(preaggregate)` rollup when its grain keeps the join's key (`grain=["flight_id"]`): the join is re-pointed at the rollup for that query, so the warehouse reads one row per parent instead of every joined row (materialization v2, phase 4, A7). A grain that also keeps a joined dimension (`["flight_id", "kind"]`) answers queries grouped or filtered by `segments.kind`. Sums, mins, maxes, filtered measures and expressions of them are served, equal to live, parents with no joined rows included. Answered live, with the path report's reason: a joined field outside the grain (`GRAIN_TOO_COARSE`), a measure the rollup does not store (`MISSING_FIELD`), an aggregate the query writes over the join itself such as `segments.count()` (`COUNT_SEMANTICS`), a fan-out grain dimension or join-level measure in the joined source's rollup (`GRAIN_TOO_COARSE`), a `timezone:`, or a query source and joined source in different time zones (`TIME_ZONE`), the parent's own aggregates beside a `join_one` rollup (`COUNT_SEMANTICS`: live repeats each parent row for every joined row when the data does not keep a `join_one` unique, and the rollup holds one row per key), a gated entry point or a joined source with its own gate (`CONTRACT`), and a joined source's rollup in a `storage=` destination (`CROSS_CONNECTION`). A `count()` measure through a `join_many`, and a sum whose value is not NULL on a parent with no joined rows, are served too, since Malloy 0.0.438 (malloydata/malloy#3208, in this release) skips such a parent's row; a `min` or `max` of such a value is answered live (`COUNT_SEMANTICS`). No API enum changes. With the switch off nothing changes.

## [0.13.0] — In development: a `name=` view replaces the table its own package wrote there

Behind `PUBLISHER_MATERIALIZE` (off by default). A `#(materialize)` source built self-instructed and unversioned writes its table at `name=` itself. A later build that names its table by generation (a control plane's instructions, or `scope: version`) used to find that table in the way of its `name=` view and refuse the build, so moving a package to orchestrated builds broke them until someone dropped the table by hand. Now, when Publisher's own records show this package's committed run wrote that exact table there (same environment and package, same source, connection and destination, and no view made there since), the build goes ahead and the view replaces the table once the new generation is built: the old table is renamed aside and the view made in its place (as one transaction on DuckDB, DuckLake and Postgres), and the old table is dropped only once the run commits. A run whose commit fails or is cancelled drops the view and puts the table back, and a build after a crash puts back a table an interrupted replacement left aside. The run's `metadata.nameViews` records `replaced_own_table`; the older runs' entries for the table are marked superseded (another loaded version that served the table is rebound and answers that source live), and deleting such a run with its tables no longer reports a failed drop. The other way, a self-instructed build that finds this package's own view at its table's name replaces the view with the table (`replaced_by_table`), in the swap's or the build's transaction where the dialect allows. Any other table, a view another package made, or a view Publisher did not mark, still refuses. See docs/materialization.md, "The `name=` view".

## [0.13.0] — In development: `#@ persist` on a view

With `PUBLISHER_MATERIALIZE` on, `#@ persist` on a view stores the view's result and answers a query from it only when the query calls that view exactly (`run: src -> view`) or starts from it (`run: src -> view -> { … }`). Refinements, nests, hand-written look-alikes and calls on an extending source are answered live; the path report lists the view's table as `kind: "view"` with why it was skipped. A view that reads a given or the current time, nests while stored with `storage=`, or sits on a gated source whose gate fields it does not group by is not built, with a `persist-view-not-built` package warning. A gated source's view is served only with `PUBLISHER_MATERIALIZE_GATED_SOURCES` on, the gate grafted on the stored result. A view's answer returns each column with the annotations live's does (`#(classification)`, `#(doc)`, render tags such as `# currency`), colocated and `storage=` alike. Off (the default), nothing changes. See docs/materialization.md, "Persisted views".

## [0.13.0] — In development: a misspelt or unparseable #(materialize) is refused at publish

Behind `PUBLISHER_MATERIALIZE` (off by default). A `#(materialize)` key outside the keys it reads (`name=` misspelt `nmae=`, say) is now `materialize-unknown-key`, at severity `error` and naming the key it was likely meant to be, and a line that does not parse is `materialize-unparseable`. Both used to be `materialize-not-built` warnings. Either way the source is still not built and serves live, but a publish (`POST /packages`) that carries one is now refused. A package that is already published keeps loading with the warning. With the switch on, a misspelt route such as `#(materialise)`, `#(preaggregates)` or `# (materialize)` is an `annotation-near-miss` warning. Off, nothing changes. See [the migration guide](docs/materialization-migration.md).

## [0.13.0] — In development: `#@ preaggregate` is deprecated in materialization v2, with a migration recipe

Materialization v2 deprecates one v1 form: `#@ preaggregate` is renamed `#(preaggregate)`, which phase 4 builds. It follows the Publisher v1 plan's rule for a deprecated form: a package warning through 0.x, refused at 1.0.0, and the reader removed in 1.1. `#@ persist` itself is not deprecated, and moving to `#(materialize)` is optional.

**`#@ -persist` is not deprecated.** It is Malloy core's own opt-out, which Malloy's persistence documentation teaches, so Publisher keeps honouring it, under `#@ persist` and `#(materialize)` alike: an opted-out reader, and any source built on it, recomputes live. It gets no warning, and it is not on the path to being refused or removed.

**`#@ preaggregate` gets `deprecated-preaggregate-annotation` with the switch on**, once per measure that declares it (`model` its file, `subject` its source), now that `#(preaggregate)` is read, built and served there. It is `warn`; `#@ preaggregate` keeps working, and its rollups still build and serve. A colocated `#@ preaggregate` measure now answers with its own annotations (`#(classification)`, `#(doc)`, `# currency`), switch on or off, built or not; they were dropped from its result column before. A rollup's table is unchanged and need not be rebuilt. `publisher_deprecated_usage_total` counts it (`preaggregate_annotation`, per measure) at every load, whether or not a warning shows.

[docs/materialization-migration.md](docs/materialization-migration.md) maps each v1 form to its v2 form, with before and after Malloy, and marks which of them work today. It also covers the one rebuild a migrated source costs, because its content address moves, and what a control plane has to do.

## [0.13.0] — Stored tables no longer answer for another source, and the path report names only the tables a query read

- **Behaviour change: a package whose persisted sources collide is refused at publish.** `PERSIST_COLLISION_ENFORCE` now defaults to `true`. A publish (`POST /packages`) in which two different `#@ persist` sources resolve to one table in one destination used to succeed with a warning; it now answers 400, naming the sources and the table, and a build of such a package that is already loaded is refused before anything is written. Loading a package at startup or reload still only warns. To fix a package, give each source a distinct `name=` (the same source reached from two models shares its table legitimately and is not a collision). A deployment that must keep publishing such packages while their authors fix them can opt out with `PERSIST_COLLISION_ENFORCE=false`, which restores the warning; the colliding sources are then answered live, as below.
- **Two sources writing one table are served live.** When two different `#@ persist` sources resolve to one table in one destination (two models each persisting a source named `summary` with no `name=`, say), each build overwrites the other's and one model answered with the other model's rows, behind a warning. Neither is now served from that table: both answer live, colocated and `storage=` alike, their serve verdicts read `live` (`refused`), and the warning says so, until each has its own `name=`. With `PERSIST_COLLISION_ENFORCE=false` they still build as before.
- **The path report names only the tables the query read.** Malloy reads every bound colocated entry before it compiles, and the report counted those reads as lookups, so a `#@ -persist` reader (which recomputes live) and a colocated `#(materialize)` source (built, not served yet) were reported `servedBy: materialized` while their SQL read the warehouse. The answers were right; the report now says `live` for them.
- **A colocated table named by a reserved word is read quoted.** A colocated `#@ persist name="order"` built, then every query on it failed with a SQL syntax error, because the table was bound unquoted at load. It is now quoted for the connection's dialect, as a rebuild already bound it.
- **A model without `##! experimental.persistence` keeps answering beside a colocated table.** Once any colocated table of a package was bound, every query on a model of that package without the flag failed ("A non-empty `buildManifest` was supplied…"). Such a model has nothing for Malloy to substitute, so it is no longer handed the package's manifest.
- **In development, behind `PUBLISHER_MATERIALIZE`:** a `#(materialize)` source whose table another, different source of the package also writes is not built, with a `materialize-not-built` warning naming the other sources and saying to give each a distinct `name=` (it used to build over the other and serve its rows). This holds whether the name is the default (the source's own, with no `name=`) or two `name=`s an author chose alike, and whatever `PERSIST_COLLISION_ENFORCE` says. `#(materialize)` on a source that inherits `#@ persist` is not built either, with a warning naming the source it inherits from (it overwrote that source's plan entry and depended on itself). A `#(materialize)` source's serve verdict now follows the served copy: `serves` where the served copy reads its table, rather than `live: shadowed`; `live` with reason `served_copy` where it does not, and for a colocated `#(materialize)` source, which is not served yet.

## [0.13.0] — Publish warnings for a destination or connection that cannot hold a table, and an orchestrator can refuse the warehouse recompute

A `storage=` source that names a destination the environment does not configure used to load cleanly and only fail at build time, so the package read as healthy while every build into that destination failed and every query was answered live. It is now a publish warning, code `materialization-destination-missing`, and its serve verdict is `live` with reason `destination_missing`. A colocated source on a connection whose configured type cannot create tables gets the same treatment: code `materialization-connection-cannot-hold-table`, reason `connection_cannot_hold_table`. Neither refuses the load; the source serves live. Both are read from the environment on every package read, so configuring the destination clears the warning without a reload. Nothing is warned while `PERSIST_STORAGE_MODE` is `off` (which ignores `storage=`) or while the environment's destination or connection list is not authoritative. Today's only read-only connection type, SQL Server, is still refused by the eligibility gate and keeps its `persist-source-refused` warning; the new connection warning reads each connection's capability so it follows a type that changes.

`BuildInstructions` gains `warehouseReach` (`recompute`, the default, or `refuse`; an open string, any other value is a 400; null reads as absent) (ms2data/service#6756). Under `strictUpstreams`, a `storage=` source whose only build recomputes its stored upstreams from the source warehouse has been built and reported as `upstreamReuse: recomputed` (`strict_shape_fallback`). With `refuse`, it fails instead: its `SourceFailure.reason` carries the reason the entry would have had, `retryable` is `false`, the run error kind is `warehouse_recompute_refused`, and `publisher_storage_chained_build_total` counts it under the existing `strict_refused` outcome.
