A materialization run that was still going when the server stopped no longer holds its package's build slot forever. Such a run used to stay `PENDING` or `MANIFEST_ROWS_READY` after a restart, so every new build of that package (or of that version) answered 409 and every scheduled fire was skipped. The server now marks each such run `FAILED` with the error "Interrupted: the server restarted during this run" when its store opens, logging a warning for each, so the next build starts and the run's tables are reclaimed as any failed run's are (a `scope: version` version's own tables go when the version is archived or deleted). If that sweep itself fails, the server still starts: the error is logged at `error` and counted in `publisher_interrupted_run_sweep_failures_total`, and the runs stay unsettled until a later restart. A scheduled fire skipped because another run is active is now logged at `warn`, not `debug`, so a slot that stays held is visible.

A rebuild of a materialized table in the source's own warehouse no longer drops the served table before its replacement is in place. It used to drop the table and then rename the new one onto its name, so a failed rename lost both copies. On Postgres and DuckDB the drop and the rename now run as one transaction, so the name is never absent and a failure leaves the served table as it was; a Postgres view that depends on the served table makes the rebuild fail with the table intact, as before, rather than following it to a renamed copy. On every other warehouse it now renames the served table aside, renames the new one in, and only then drops the old copy; when the new one cannot go in, the old one is renamed back. Between the two renames the name is briefly absent, so a query landing there fails rather than reading a partial table, and a crash there leaves the old copy under a backup name that the next build of the source restores or drops. That path issues one more statement per rebuild than before, the drop of the old copy, and probes for the served table (`SELECT 1 FROM … WHERE 1 = 0`) only when moving it aside fails for a reason other than its absence, aborting the swap when the probe fails too. A rebuild into a storage destination now creates and reads back the table in one transaction, so a failed read-back rolls back to the previous generation instead of dropping the table a committed manifest still serves from.

**`/entities` reads every gate the server accepts.** A source gated by an expression that starts with a string literal, such as `#(authorize) "admin" = $ROLE`, used to be reported as locked (`false`) by `GET …/packages/{pkg}/entities`, because its reader took the leading quote for the legacy quoted-string form. It now reports the gate as written, telling the two forms apart the way the load does: only a payload that is one string literal is the legacy form.

**Deprecated: `GET /environments/{env}?reload=true`.** It re-reads the environment's block of `publisher.config.json`; no first-party client calls it, and the v1 API has no environment reload. A response to it now carries `Deprecation: true`, and each use is counted in `publisher_deprecated_usage_total{feature="environment_reload"}`. It is removed once that count reads zero ([#1540](https://github.com/malloydata/publisher/issues/1540)). It still works, and under `frozenConfig` it is still refused like any change to an environment. To pick up a package's changed files, reload the package.

## [0.12.5] — `--help` and the configuration reference come from the settings registry, and startup logs the settings given

Every setting is described once, in the settings registry 0.12.2 added, and three things are now generated from it:

- **`--help`** lists every flag the server reads, with what it sets and its default. It used to leave out `--serving-api-enabled`, `--no-serving-api-enabled`, `--admin-api-enabled` and `--no-admin-api-enabled`.
- **The table of variables in `docs/configuration.md`**, which CI checks against the registry. It gains the rows the hand-written table lacked: `PUBLISHER_CONFIG_PATH`, `PERSIST_COLLISION_ENFORCE`, `PUBLISHER_MCP_TRACE`, `PUBLISHER_QUERY_METADATA`, `PUBLISHER_BYPASS_AUTHORIZE_SECRET`, and the admin storage key, secret, region and endpoint.
- **A startup line naming each setting a flag, a variable or the file gave**, with its value and where it came from, such as `Settings given: port=4100 from PUBLISHER_PORT, mcp.port=4141 from --mcp_port`. A setting given its default value is listed too. Secrets and `PUBLISHER_ADMIN_STORAGE_KEY_ID` show as `(set)`, and a URL's user and password as `***`, as in `https://***@minio:9000`. A structured setting (`theme`, `environments`, `retrieval`) shows only where it came from. With nothing given, the line says every setting is at its default.

## [0.12.4] — `#(classification)` and `#(carries)` are additive: gates load as in 0.11, `#(carries)` refuses only what it can reach, every query route writes an access record, and the compliance review separates what it could not check from what failed (BREAKING)

`#(classification)` and `#(carries)` add to a package and change nothing about the tags already there. `#(authorize)`, `#(access_filter)` and givens load and serve as they did in 0.11 whether or not either new tag appears in the package, including a package 0.12.0 refused for a gate on a plain given. Only `#(carries)` refuses, and only for what a query or a source can reach; `#(classification)` labels and warns.

`#(carries)` and `#(classification)` are a preview. This release closes many of the shapes 0.12.0 served past a `#(carries)` list, but not all of them yet; [docs/classification.md](docs/classification.md#known-gaps) lists the ones still open. Treat a `#(carries)` list as a review aid, not an enforcement boundary, until they close.

A package that declares `#(carries)` is held to more. 0.12.0 loaded some such packages whose `#(carries)` lists did not hold. These now refuse the load, as a gate that does not parse does: a 400 on publish and reload, an entry in `loadErrors` otherwise. Each message names the source, the field or join, and the fix. A package that loaded on 0.12.0 and trips one of these does not load after upgrade, so run the package through a reload before rolling out.

- A view on a `#(carries)` source: A view returns what it groups by, aggregates and filters on, so a view that reads a class the source does not carry, a field with no class, or a field the view declares itself with `extend:` refuses the load. A view with no reference summary refuses too. Remove the view, or declare the field on the source with a `#(classification)` and read it from there.
- A `->` query source, or a join hidden from discovery, on a `#(carries)` source: A source defined as `base -> { ... }` carries the classes of what its query reads, and a field read through a hidden join carries the class declared where it lives. A leak through either refuses the load, where 0.12.0 did not look.
- A passthrough relabel that declares a lower class: `dimension: year_only is birth_year` with `#(classification) "none"` over a field classified `phi.quasi_identifier` refuses under `#(carries)`: a plain copy, with or without a cast, does not de-identify anything. Remove the declaration so the copy keeps its input's class, or derive a new field with a function that does. A relabelled copy now passes its input's classes on, so a field or view reading the copy carries them too. A field whose read cannot be resolved against the source refuses as well; declare a `#(classification)` on it. An output Publisher cannot follow to what it reads, such as a `nest:` with stages of its own, refuses whatever it declares: flatten the nest into one stage, or move it out of the source. A plain copy declared lower is refused wherever a `#(carries)` reaches it, whether or not the copied class is on the list. That covers a copy in a carried source an open source joins, and a copy the joining entry re-declares itself, at load and per query.
- Joins past 16 deep or 1024 paths: Where Publisher cannot read past that bound it refuses a `#(carries)` source whose fields it cannot all read, rather than assume the rest is safe. Drop the joins past the bound, or split the source. The join-bypass check hits the same bound and warns that a gate may sit unread past it.
- A join to a source locked to a term the entry does not require: Lock terms are compared by given, operator and decoded literal, so `'clinician' in $ROLES` matches `"clinician" in $ROLES`. An author join from a source locked to `'analyst' in $ROLES` to one locked to `'admin' in $ROLES` warns `join-bypass`, because every analyst would read the admin source's rows. The grammar has no OR. To serve the broader role, join an extension of the joined source that declares the entry's own lock, or add the term to the entry's `#(authorize)`. A join to a source locked `#(authorize) false` warns only from an ungated entry; a gated entry over a locked base is the curated-extension pattern and draws no warning.
- A query on a `#(carries)` source reads past its list (BREAKING for those queries): `#(carries)` is also checked per query, on the fields the compiled query reads. A caller's own `extend:`, a join it writes (its `on` counts), a source it declares over the carried one, a filter, a nest or an `internal:` column it reads through `extend` is refused with a 400 unless every field it reads has a class on the list; the refusal is recorded as `bad_request` with the `fieldsRead`. A read through a join to a `#(carries)` source is held to that source's list even from an entry that carries none, and a `->` query source is held to the strictest list along its own chain and its base's, at load and per query. A caller cannot write `#(classification)` or `#(carries)` in query text. Named queries and notebook cells on a `#(carries)` source that read past the list now refuse the package load. Classify what a caller should read, or add the class to the list. The check runs on a query that can reach a `#(carries)`, including one it reaches only through an import, a join or a `compose` member, and an `index:` query that can reach one returns a 400. A name Publisher cannot resolve counts as reaching one.
- A query source's `extend:`, `nest:` and joined outputs: The `#(carries)` check now follows a field a `base -> { ... }` source declares with `extend:`, the outputs of a `nest:` in the query, and a joined query source's outputs. A filter in the query is charged its class on its own, so an output that inherits a declared class is no longer refused as a "plain copy" of a field the filter reads, and its class reaches every field and view that reads the output, including through a hidden one. A hidden computed field that declares a class below its inputs now warns `classification-downgrade` whenever a published field or view reads it, directly or through other fields.
- Later `->` stages: A stage whose `extend:` re-declares a name the source or an earlier stage already has is refused as unreadable only when either meaning carries a class or a ceiling; two plain ones are served. A caller join's `on` in a later stage is read against that stage's own names, so a name an earlier stage output resolves.
- Record and array dimensions: A record (`{ v is ssn }`), an array (`[ssn]`), a record nested in either, and a nest output read whole are each held to `#(carries)` by what they read, at load and per query, wherever they are declared: on the carried source, in a caller's `extend:`, in a `->` stage, or on a joined source. 0.12.0 skipped them, so a query could return a classified value inside a record. Each part of a computed record carries the record's classes, and a record whose part cannot be resolved refuses. The access record now lists what a record read.
- `->` pipeline joins: A join written inside a `->` query source's pipeline is walked the same way as a declared join.
- Hidden sources under `queryableSources: "all"`: The load checks (`#(carries)`, and the join-bypass warnings) now read every top-level source in every model, since a hidden source answers a query by name there. A package that set `"all"` and carried a `#(carries)` gap in a hidden source refuses.
- A PATCH that changes what is queryable: Changing `explores` or `queryableSources` through `PATCH` re-runs the load gates against the new surface and refuses the change when a gate fails, rather than serving it. A PATCH that also names a new `location` runs the gates on the new tree under the new listing before the swap commits, so a refusal leaves the old tree serving and its location recorded. A PATCH that changes neither skips the walk. The new listing goes live only after the gates pass: a query that arrives while they run is served under the old one, and a gate that refuses or fails leaves the old listing in place.

  0.12.0 also refused the load of a package whose `#(authorize)` or `#(access_filter)` read a given not declared `#(secure)`. That refusal is removed, and a package it rejected loads again. A plain given is whatever the caller of the API supplies, and a deployment whose trusted tier sets its givens from its own verified context has a real gate on it. `#(secure)` is a marker for whoever calls Publisher: protect this given from your own clients, setting it yourself rather than passing a client's value through. Only a `#(secure)` given hides a source from discovery, and the access record still logs a plain given's name but never its value.

The access record covered only `POST …/models/{path}/query` in 0.12.0. It now covers every route that runs a query: REST, the legacy notebook cell route, MCP `execute_query` (a refused argument included, and the package `version` that answered), `get_context` value lookups, and raw SQL against a connection (`/sqlQuery` and `/sqlTemporaryTable`), which is recorded as `decision: "ungated"` because no gate runs on it. The value-index build at package load is the system's own read, not a caller's, and writes no record. A request writes exactly one record whether it succeeds, is refused before or inside the model, times out, or is abandoned by the client (`outcome: "cancelled"`, status 499). Fields added: `fieldsReadComplete` (false when a read could not be placed or the join walk was cut short), `dropped` on a field read (classes its inputs carry that it declares below), `connection` on raw SQL, and `caller` and `traceId` on the MCP routes. The error text is redacted of credentials a driver quotes back and capped at 2000 characters. Materialization builds run as the system and are not recorded. See [docs/access-record.md](docs/access-record.md).

The access record's `error` now carries a connection error's HTTP-answer text, not the driver's, since a driver quotes the statement back and a plain given's value is a literal in it; a request refused before its controller runs (a bad `includeHiddenFilesAndSources`, a bad notebook-cell parameter, the concurrency cap) now writes its one record; and a failure to build or emit a record is logged and never replaces the query's answer or error.

A join that bypasses a gate is a `join-bypass` warning in every package, in `warnings` and `get_status`; the server no longer refuses it anywhere, and a `PATCH` re-gate loads it the same way. That is looser than 0.12.0, which refused it in a package that declared `#(carries)` or `#(classification)`; 0.11 had no such check. A gate governs the source a query enters through, so an author join from a broader entry to a stricter source is the author's choice of what that entry exposes, and the warning asks whether it was meant (see [docs/authorize.md](docs/authorize.md#gates-are-edge-controls)). The hard stop is now the compliance review: `compliance.py` fails `loads:join` on each warning, so run it in CI for any package that must not expose one. A finding names the source the join reaches. The check follows a `->` source to the source it derives from and a `compose` source to its resolved member, and a query that reaches a `#(carries)` source is refused when its join fan-out exceeds 1024 paths or it is an `index:` query, since neither can be read to a ceiling.

`#(carries)` no longer refuses a query or a named query that cannot reach a carried source, even in a model that declares one.

A computed field that declares a class below the fields its expression reads now loads with a `classification-downgrade` warning, since Publisher cannot tell whether the expression de-identifies. `GET …/packages/{pkg}` `warnings` and `get_status` carry it, and a review treats it as a finding. Under `#(carries)` the same declaration on a plain copy refuses, as above.

`compliance.py` (the `malloy-compliance-review` skill) now reports what it could not check apart from what failed:

- A probe is refused when the server answers 403, or 404 with the query boundary's own refusal. Any other non-2xx, such as a 400 from a typo or a 401, never reached the gate and needs review instead of counting as a refusal.
- A gated domain is also probed with no givens at all (`{}`) and must refuse.
- A scope in the register that names no published domain, declared source or refusal kind fails as an unknown scope. A `caps` entry takes `min` as well as `max`, and a capped field that was not profiled needs review.
- `locked_bases` needs review, rather than passing, when `--package-dir` is not a package (holds no `publisher.json`): the server answers a model kept off the surface and a missing one alike, so only the package's own directory makes that 404 a refusal. A domain gated only by a row filter may answer the no-givens probe with no rows. A scope on `coverage`, `gated`, `secure_gates`, `ceiling` or `values` must name a published domain, so a renamed one fails as an unknown scope.
- Exit codes: 0 every control holds, 1 a control fails, 2 usage, 3 nothing failed but something needs review, 4 internal error. Pass `--allow-review` to turn 3 into 0 where a person triages review items. A pipeline that failed only on exit 1 should now fail on any non-zero code, or pass `--allow-review`.
- `--mcp` is required when `--server` is not localhost.
- A package the server does not serve and names no load error for is a review item (exit 3), since nothing was checked.

In `examples/clinical-records`, the de-identified patient now returns a null `birth_year` past age 89, the research register caps `patient.birth_year` at a minimum of 1930, and `violations/06-birth-year-over-89` seeds the failure. A package copied from the earlier example keeps publishing the year of birth for every age until it makes the same change.

## [0.12.3] — `POST …/packages?dryRun=true` loads and checks a package without installing it

`?dryRun=true` on a publish loads the tree at `location` and runs the publish checks exactly as a publish would, then discards it and closes its connections, as any load that fails now does too. The answer is what a publish would answer for that tree: the same 400 or 424 refusal, or 200 with the package as it would load, `warnings` included, and the `location` it came from. With package versioning on it also requires a valid `version` in the tree's `publisher.json`, and refuses a `description` that is not a string or a `manifestLocation` that names no manifest, as a versioned publish does; the 200 names the version as `versionId`. Nothing is installed, served or listed, and the package already served under the name is untouched, so a CI gate can ask "would this publish?" of a branch head without exposing its content. Version lifecycle checks (an existing version, `latest`) are not part of it. A frozen configuration and memory backpressure refuse a dry run as they refuse a publish, and memory is checked again after the download. A server runs at most 2 at once; more are refused with 503. `publisher_package_dry_run_duration{outcome}` times each one (`loaded`, `refused`, `backpressure`, `at_capacity`, `failed`); a dry run's load is not counted in the package load metrics, deprecated-usage counts or entities findings of the package it names, and a failed one logs at info, not as a load error.

## [0.12.3] — Compile takes a `files` overlay, so an author's tool can check unsaved edits

`POST …/models/{path}/compile` (scopes `file` and `package`) takes an optional `files`: a list of `{ path, content }` `.malloy` and `.malloynb` files read instead of, or beside, the package's own for that one request. An entry naming a package file replaces it, and one naming a new file adds it, so an import of it resolves. Nothing is written to disk, cached, or seen by another request: the overlay is served to the compiler by file URL and dropped with the request. `/query` takes no overlay; a query runs against the package as served.

- **An empty `files` is no overlay:** the request is an ordinary one.
- **Scopes.** At `file`, the model in the URL and everything it imports read the overlaid text, and an entry for the model itself may stand in for `source` (giving both is a 400). At `package`, every file compiles as a reload would, overlaid files new to the package included. Each problem names its file (`model`) and its position in that file's text, so a tool can show each file's errors without saving. `files` at scope `append` is a 400: append checks text against the package as published.
- **Overlay files are package files.** They are not restricted like ad-hoc text, and their `#(authorize)` and `#(access_filter)` annotations gate as written, including ones they add, change or remove. A host must offer `files` only to callers who may edit the package (see `docs/authorize.md`). `source` text beside an overlay is still caller text and may not declare a gate.
- **Bounds.** At most 500 files and 8 MiB of text per request; past either is a 413. A path that is absolute, has a `.` or `..` segment or a backslash, names a file other than a model or notebook, or appears twice is a 400. Data files and `publisher.json` are read from the package as published. The compile route accepts a request body up to twice the byte bound plus 1 MiB, rather than the server's usual 1 MiB.
- **Telemetry.** `publisher_request_overlay_total{outcome}` counts compile requests that carried an overlay (`accepted`, `refused_entry`, `refused_bounds`).

## [0.12.2] — Settings are read once, from one registry, and bad values fail startup

Every Publisher setting is now read once at startup, through one registry, as step 1 of the configuration design (now Appendix C of [docs/publisher-v1.md](docs/publisher-v1.md#appendix-c-the-configuration-registry-and-mapping)) lays out. The names, the defaults and the precedence are today's, and no value that works changes meaning. These are the changes:

- **A value that does not parse fails startup**, and every bad value of one startup is reported together, one line each, in one format: `mcp.port from MCP_PORT: expected an integer from 0 to 65535, got "40a0"`. A value used to fail only when something read it, sometimes on the first query; it now fails even for a setting this configuration never reads, such as a memory-governor fraction with `PUBLISHER_MAX_MEMORY_BYTES` unset. Some values that used to be accepted are now refused, because each setting has one type:
  - `PUBLISHER_PORT`, `MCP_PORT`, `SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_DURATION_SECONDS` and `SHUTDOWN_GRACEFUL_CLOSE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` were read with `Number()` and no check, so a typo was `NaN` and a fraction was accepted. They now take whole numbers in decimal digits, so `SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_DURATION_SECONDS=2.5`, `SHUTDOWN_GRACEFUL_CLOSE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=2.5` and `PUBLISHER_PORT=4000.0` fail. Under Bun, a non-numeric `MCP_PORT` bound an ephemeral port. `0` is still an ephemeral port.
  - `PACKAGE_LOAD_JOB_TIMEOUT_MS` fell back to 120000 on any bad value. `PACKAGE_LOAD_WORKERS` read `5abc` as 5.
  - `PUBLISHER_RATE_LIMIT`, `PUBLISHER_ADMIN_PORT` and `PACKAGE_LOAD_SCHEMA_CACHE_BYTES` accepted whatever `Number()` reads (`1e3`, `0x10`, `4100.0`). They now take decimal digits.
  - `PUBLISHER_MCP_TRACE` read anything but `retrieval` as off.
  - `PUBLISHER_ALLOW_UNVERIFIED_SSH_HOST_KEY` read an unrecognised value as off where a tunnel connected, and refused it only when a connection's config loaded.
  - `mcp.includeHiddenFilesAndSources` in publisher.config.json ignored a value that is not a boolean, with a warning. A value that spells no boolean (`"enabled"`, `1`) now fails.
  - `frozenConfig` in publisher.config.json was read with `Boolean()`, so `1` froze the server and `0` did not. In the file a boolean is `true` or `false`, so a number now fails.
  - `PUBLISHER_PACKAGE_VERSIONING`, `PUBLISHER_VERSION_PROMOTION`, `PUBLISHER_MODEL_PAGE` and `versionPromotion` in publisher.config.json, given a value outside their set, failed the environments' initialization: the server stayed up and `/status` named the value in `initError`. They now stop startup, as every other bad value does. `PUBLISHER_PACKAGE_INLINE_FIELDS` already stopped it, and now names the setting in the same format as the rest.
- **An empty variable, or one of only spaces, is unset for every setting, and values are trimmed.** `PACKAGE_LOAD_WORKERS=""` used to fail startup. It now takes the default. A few values of only spaces used to mean something, and now take the default too: `PUBLISHER_PORT` and `MCP_PORT` bound an ephemeral port, `PUBLISHER_CONFIG_PATH` loaded no config, and `"frozenConfig": " "` froze the server. `LOG_LEVEL=" info"` is now `info`, not an unknown level, and the `PUBLISHER_ADMIN_STORAGE_*` key, secret, region and endpoint are trimmed.
- **The config file's settings take effect on restart.** `frozenConfig` was read again at every `/status` and theme request, and `versionPromotion` at every publish, so an edit to either took effect without a restart. Both are now read once at startup, as every other setting already was.
- **A config file that cannot be read or parsed fails startup**, with the reason and `PUBLISHER_INIT_FAILED` on stderr, before anything binds. Before, the server started with `frozenConfig` off and both APIs on, and named the problem only on `/status`.
- **Flags no longer set environment variables.** Each flag used to write its variable into the environment, so a `${SERVER_ROOT}` or `${PUBLISHER_PORT}` in publisher.config.json resolved to the flag's value, the Docker image's `--server_root /publisher` included. A `${VAR}` now resolves only to a variable that is set, so such a reference with only the flag given is reported as not set.
- **Booleans keep their meaning, and the spellings that would change it are warned about.** `INITIALIZE_STORAGE`, `PUBLISHER_USE_BUNDLED_DEFAULT` and `PUBLISHER_ALLOW_PROXY_CONNECTIONS` are on only for exactly `true`. `DISABLE_RESPONSE_LOGGING` is on only for `true` or `1`. `"frozenConfig": "false"` freezes the server. Each of these still means what it did, and startup now warns about any value another boolean setting would read differently (`INITIALIZE_STORAGE=1`, `PUBLISHER_ALLOW_PROXY_CONNECTIONS=yes`, `"frozenConfig": "false"`). A later release refuses those values, so write `true` or `false`. A value no boolean reads (`enabled`) fails startup now.
- **Startup warns about what used to be ignored.** That covers an unknown key in publisher.config.json (naming the nearest known key, so `adminApiEnable` points at `adminApiEnabled`), an unknown flag, a flag given without its value, and an invalid `LOG_LEVEL`, which still falls back to `debug`.

## [0.12.2] — The model viewer says when it can't tell whether a source reads a given, names a run's givens as its controls do, and lists a givens-only model's givens

On a server with `PUBLISHER_MODEL_PAGE=viewer`:

- **Givens it can't tie to a source.** The viewer finds which givens a source reads in the model file's text, so it can't see what a source declared in another file reads, or what a source here builds on from one. It still shows and sends those givens, so a run never goes out without one it needs, and now says which they are: the Givens section says a value set for one may not apply to this source, and a run's card says it ran with those values only where the source reads them. A given the source's own text reads is known to apply, whatever the source is built on. A named query the model gives no source is read the same way: when it runs over something the model doesn't hold, every given goes with it, and its card says which it can't tie to the query. A run held only for such givens offers **Run anyway**: it runs without them, and its card says so.
- **Plain words.** A run's card names the values it ran with the way the Givens controls word them (`Ordered since: Jan 1, 2023`, `Category: All`), not as Malloy literals (`SINCE = @2023-01-01`, `CATEGORY = f''`), and in full: every picked value, never cut to a button's width. A missing given is named by its label.
- **A givens-only model** lists its givens (name, label, type, default, description) under "This model defines no sources or queries.", rather than showing nothing, and says which of them it imports rather than declares.

## [0.12.2] — `PUBLISHER_MODEL_PAGE=viewer` takes the Explorer out of the Console

The Console's model page embeds the Malloy Explorer, which turns a structured query back into Malloy text with `ASTQuery.toMalloy()`, and `@malloydata/malloy-interfaces` writes a string value into that text unescaped: its `escapeString` is still a TODO. A value holding a double quote therefore ends the string early. Drilling into a result cell holding `27" Monitor` sends `drill: name = "27" Monitor"`, which fails to compile, and drilling into a cell holding `x" or "a" = "a` sends a filter that matches every row. Nobody has to type the quote: it only has to be in the data. The Explorer's filter box is not affected, because a typed filter is a filter expression, which upstream quotes correctly. The server bounds all of it: caller text compiles in restricted mode and the `#(authorize)` gates apply to whatever runs, so no query reaches data its caller could not already query.

A new server setting, `PUBLISHER_MODEL_PAGE`, picks the model page: `explorer`, the default, keeps the Explorer, so nothing changes until a deployment opts in; `viewer` shows a page that builds no query. On `viewer`, the model page is the model viewer, in the next section, and a legacy `.malloynb` notebook's import cell no longer offers the "Data sources" dialog, which is the same Explorer. Any other value fails startup. It is a lasting setting: the Console keeps both pages.

**Server.** `/status` reports the setting as `modelPage` (`explorer` or `viewer`). A server that predates it sends no field, which reads as `explorer`.

**SDK.** `Model` shows the page the server names, and nothing until `/status` answers, so a `viewer` server never flashes the Explorer. That includes a retry paused offline or in a hidden tab: `useServer().isLoadingStatus` now stays true until `/status` has answered or failed. `/status` is retried, and when it still cannot be read the Console shows the viewer, the page that writes no value into Malloy: a deployment that chose `viewer` never gets the Explorer back from one failed request. It is cached per server, so two `ServerProvider`s on different servers each read their own. `useServer()` gains `modelPage`, and the type `ModelPage` is exported. Every export stays, the Explorer's among them. `ModelExplorer`, `ModelExplorerDialog` and `SourcesExplorer` ignore the setting, so a host that draws one checks `modelPage` first. ESLint refuses `@malloydata/malloy-explorer`, `@malloydata/malloy-query-builder`, and `queryToMalloy` and `filterToMalloy` from `@malloydata/malloy-interfaces`, in the SDK and the Console, outside the Explorer's own files, and any reach for a `toMalloy` member. Only the pages that check the setting may import the SDK's Explorer modules or its query builder's loader.

## [0.12.2] — With `PUBLISHER_MODEL_PAGE=viewer`, the model page is the model viewer, ported from the Credible app

On a server started with `PUBLISHER_MODEL_PAGE=viewer`, opening a `.malloy` file in the Console shows one source at a time, picked from an "N sources" pill beside its name, with the model's and the source's docs and its access rules under it. Then, as page sections: the givens the source reads, set once for every run below them, a picker reading its options only when it is opened; its views and the model's named queries, each of which runs when it is opened and never on render, with its Malloy one click over; its measures, calculations, dimensions and joins, each opening to its Malloy, read from the model file. A dimension tagged `#(index)` or `#(index_values)` lists its most common values, from one capped `group_by` query. A join opens to the joined source's fields. Nothing is sent until a reader opens a row or a picker. The source and the given values are in the address (`?source=`, `?REGION=West`), so a link, and Copy link, opens on what the page was running with; a link that carried given values for the Explorer page still applies them. The default, `explorer`, keeps the Explorer page as it was.

It is the Credible app's model viewer, moved into the SDK so the Console and the Credible app draw the same page. What only the Credible platform knows (what it has built from a model, its own index of a dimension's values, generated descriptions, downloads) stays in the Credible app, which adds it back through the viewer's props.

**SDK.** New: `ModelViewer` and its props, `malloyIdentifier`, and `modelQueryKey` and `runQueryKey` (the viewer's cache keys). On a `viewer` server, `Model` is `ModelViewer` with a Copy link action, and takes every `ModelViewer` prop (`givens` and `onGivensChange` among them, as before). The Explorer page reads only `resourceUri`, `maxResultSize`, `givens` and `onGivensChange`, besides its own `onChange` and `runOnDemand`, so the viewer's other props do nothing on an `explorer` server. A host that wants the viewer whatever the server says renders `ModelViewer` itself. The host-facing parts are **experimental** and may change in a minor release until a host has been built on them: the `ModelViewerExtensions` slots (`renderRunActions`, `fetchSamples` and `samplesGeneration`, `renderFieldStatus`, `renderFieldAction`, `renderFieldDetail`, `showField`, `renderSourceDetail`, `describePickerSource`), and the `entities`, `entitiesError`, `joinHref` and `columnDescriptions` props, with `FieldEntity` and `groupEntitiesBySource`. The viewer writes no value into Malloy text: a run is a view or a query by name, every name is backtick-quoted with its own backslashes and backticks escaped, and given values travel as the request's `givens`. A run, and a dimension's sample read, sends only the values of the givens its source reads, so changing another source's given leaves an open result current. Which givens a source reads is found in the model file's text, so a source built on something the file doesn't declare (an imported source, a query, a `compose(…)`) shows, and sends, every given. `useGivenUrlParams` gains `setParam`, for a host's own parameter (the source on screen) written the same way as the givens: in place, keeping the fragment, and without dropping a given written in the same tick.

**Option lists.** On a `viewer` server, and in the model viewer wherever it is drawn, a given's `suggest { source=… dimension=… }` query backtick-quotes the source's and the dimension's names, so a name that is a Malloy keyword (`year`, `source`) no longer fails the picker's list. `buildSuggestQuery` takes `{ quoteNames }` for it, and `useSuggestOptions` a trailing `quoteNames`. On the default server a suggest query is written as before.

**Releasing.** This adds a server setting and a new SDK component with its own API, so cut it as a minor release, not the default patch.

## [0.12.2] — A "Contains" dimension filter matches the text it was given, and a filter given keeps its escapes

The SDK writes a few filters as Malloy text itself, and two of them wrote values the filter grammar then misread. A "Contains" dimension filter (`DimensionFilter`, `useDimensionFilters`, `useDimensionFiltersQuery`, `generateFilterClause`, and the other dimensions' value lists `useDimensionalFilterRangeData` reads under it) spliced its value into `f'%…%'`, where `,` separates alternatives and `%` and `_` are wildcards: "a,b" matched values ending in `a` or starting with `b` and not "a,b" itself, "50%" also matched "500", and "x_y" also matched "xzy". It is now printed by `@malloydata/malloy-filter`, so it matches exactly the text typed. And `malloyLiteral` doubled every backslash in a `filter<…>` value, which undid the filter's own escapes: a multi-pick holding "a,b", carried as `a\,b`, ran as "a\" or "b" when a report or document applied it as a literal. It now hands the value through unchanged and escapes only a bare quote.

Neither path goes through `@malloydata/malloy-interfaces`, whose `escapeString` is still unfixed upstream; these are the SDK's own text, now covered by tests that parse what they write. The value lists also wrote a date bound on Greater Than and Less Than as the Date's text rather than as a day; they now write `@2024-01-05`, as the result rows' query does.

## [0.12.1] — `Package` carries the package's own fields; what an indexer reads, the build plan and the semantic index state move to their own routes, and serving state to `GET …/packages/{pkg}/status`

A package response now describes the package. What was computed onto it moves to where it is read, so a listing and the `/status` poll stop carrying per-model data for every package, and each fact has one home:

| Was on `Package`                                                                                                                                                     | Now                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `buildPlan`                                                                                                                                                          | `GET …/packages/{pkg}/build-plan`: the plan itself; empty when the package declares no persist source, 409 `BUILD_PLAN_UNAVAILABLE` when it could not be derived                          |
| `embeddingIndex`                                                                                                                                                     | `GET …/packages/{pkg}/embedding-index`                                                                                                                                                    |
| `agents`                                                                                                                                                             | `GET …/packages/{pkg}/agents` (unchanged route)                                                                                                                                           |
| `secureGivens`                                                                                                                                                       | `GET …/packages/{pkg}/entities`: each model's `givens` carries `secure` (`.malloy` models; a given declared only in a notebook is not listed)                                             |
| `status`, `loaded`, `archiveStatus`, `servedRevision`, `sourceContentSha`, `manifestBindingStatus`, `manifestEntryCount`, `boundManifestUri`, `storageServeBindings` | `GET …/packages/{pkg}/status`, the package's serving state; `GET /status` keeps what a reconcile reads (`status`, `loaded`, `archiveStatus`, `manifestBindingStatus`, `boundManifestUri`) |

`warnings`, `exploresWarnings` and the package's identity, description and configuration stay on `Package` and its listings. A `GET /status` entry is a `PackageStatusEntry`: only what a reconcile reads, so the poll no longer computes each package's warnings. While `PUBLISHER_PACKAGE_INLINE_FIELDS` is on, an entry is the full package response, and the schema declares it so (`allOf` `Package`). A `?reload=true` response always carries `servedRevision` and `sourceContentSha`, the reload's receipt.

`classification`, which 0.12.0 added to the single-package read, moves to `GET …/packages/{pkg}/classification` (`sources` empty when nothing published is classified). It stays on the single-package read, deprecated, under the same flag.

**Nothing breaks in this release.** The moved fields are marked deprecated and stay on every package response while `PUBLISHER_PACKAGE_INLINE_FIELDS` is `on`, the default. Turn it `off` to serve only the package's own fields and check your callers read the new homes. A later release turns it off by default, and the one after removes the fields and the setting.

**New: `GET …/packages/{pkg}/entities`** returns, for each `.malloy` model, what an indexer reads from it. By default it follows the rules of `GET …/models/{path}`: only the files on the package's surface, and no source locked with `#(authorize) false`; `includeHiddenFilesAndSources=true` returns every file and source, for a host that indexes them. Per model: each source's public fields (kind, type, declaring code, annotations, `#(doc)` text, table, what a join joins, and for an `#(index)` dimension its `indexFingerprint`), the facts the model states about each source (doc, `#(agent-hidden)`, whether this server queries it directly and which served source stands for it, `#(filter)`s, effective `#(authorize)`/`#(access_filter)` gates with their `field <op> $GIVEN` terms), the model's givens and each source's schema. An `#(index)` dimension's fingerprint is the SHA-256 of the SQL its canonical index query compiles to, plus the dimensions that partition it, so a host can reuse one index across versions that compile a dimension the same way. It is computed once at load from the models as compiled before any manifest is bound; a model with no entities has `error` and `errorKind` (`compile` for the author's compile error, `extraction` for the server's failure to extract it). Givens are serialized as every other route serializes them, `required` included. `#(filter)`s are read as the query path reads them, an extending source overriding its base's by name. A host that indexes packages no longer compiles each one a second time.

**The load warns about annotations an index cannot honor**, and still loads the package: a required `#(filter)` on a dimension that does not exist or is not public, or an `#(index)` on a field that is not a dimension, on a source with a required parameter, with more than one author-declared required filter, or with a `sharing=` or `schedule=` key. Each is one package warning with a stable `code` (`entities-not-a-dimension`, `entities-parameterized-source`, `entities-multiple-required-filters`, `entities-sharing-not-allowed-on-dimension`, `entities-schedule-not-allowed-on-dimension`, `entities-required-filter-missing-dimension`, `entities-required-filter-non-public-dimension`) and a message that says what to change; the annotation is left out of `/entities` (no fingerprint, no filter). A host that indexes can refuse a publish on those codes. `POST …/compile` at scope `package` reports them too, and `publisher_package_entities_findings_total{reason}` counts them. An `#(index)` on a non-public field is skipped silently.

## [0.12.1] — get_context lists environments and packages, so an agent can find data with it alone

`get_context` no longer requires `search_targets` or `scopes`. A call without targets lists, one level at a time, in the shapes the hosted retrieval API uses:

- No arguments: `listing: "environments"`, each with how many packages it serves.
- `environment`: `listing: "packages"`, each with the first line of its description as `one_line_summary`.
- A package in `scopes`: its sources, plus `package_info` with the package's full description.
- A source in `scopes`: its fields.

A level with only one choice is entered rather than listed, and a warning says so. So on a server serving one package, a call with no arguments returns that package's sources, and a search with no `scopes` searches it, unless an environment could not be read or another package is still loading, when the search is refused and asks for the package by name. A search still needs one package: with several, it is refused with a `Fix:` naming them, because each package is indexed on its own. A package that failed to load, or is still loading, is named in a warning rather than listed, and a listing too long for one response is cut, with a warning saying how many it left out; `list_packages` still reports every package with its load error.

## [0.12.0] - A DuckLake catalog given as fields uses its own `sslmode`

A DuckLake connection's `catalog.postgresConnection` given as fields (host, port, database, user, password) now applies its `sslmode`, where before the field was ignored and the catalog took the deployment's `PGSSLMODE`. A worker running `PGSSLMODE=allow` therefore no longer tries plaintext first against a catalog that sets `no-verify` (sent to libpq as `require`), `verify-ca` or `verify-full`. A catalog with no `sslmode`, and one given as a `connectionString`, build exactly as before, and the catalog still gets no statement timeout. **A catalog that already carried an `sslmode` changes behaviour on upgrade**: the value now applies, and `disable` is the sharpest case, since under `PGSSLMODE=require` it now connects in plaintext. The load also checks the value: an `sslmode` outside `disable | no-verify | verify-ca | verify-full`, or `verify-ca` with no readable CA bundle, rejects the connection (or, as a storage destination, that destination alone) instead of failing at every attach. Attached databases made the same change earlier (PR 1292).

## [0.12.0] — get_context has one search engine (BREAKING)

Every ranked `get_context` request is now answered by the find, list, judge engine, for every package: it ranks each target against the whole package (embedding closeness, keyword match and stored values, fused by rank), shows a model the best candidates grouped by source with the join routes between them, and returns what the model picks. A request with no `search_text` is still a listing and is unchanged. The engine's settings are under `retrieval.fcj` in `publisher.json`; the defaults now put it in list mode (`connect: "list"`) with `listTopK: 30`, `listUnion: 30`, `dropRoutesAt: 4` and `readingsRule: true`, and `docs/configuration.md` describes them.

The earlier search is gone, and so are its settings. `representation`, `keyphrases`, `refine`, `rerank`, `sourceMatch` and the prompts `keyphrase`, `refine`, `rerank` and `sourceMatch` in `publisher.json` no longer do anything. A package that still sets them loads, the keys are ignored, and the package's `warnings` name each one; remove them. `retrieval.indexing.maxEntities` in `publisher.config.json` is ignored the same way, with a warning at startup, and `EMBEDDING_MIN_SIMILARITY` now applies to `search_database_schema` only. A response now also carries `clusters`, `coverage`, `unresolved_targets` and `engine`, and a long answer pages with `offset` and `next_offset`.

The request is unchanged, so an agent's calls still work. What can break, for an agent or a client that reads the response:

- `below_cutoff_count` and `total_entities` are gone from the response.
- The `retrieval_reason` values `too-many-entities` and `cooldown` are no longer produced.
- A failed judge call fails the request with `retrieval_reason: "llm-stage-failed"` rather than answering without it (set `retrieval.fcj.judge` to `false` to answer without the judge).
- A server with no embedding key answers ranked requests with `retrieval: "lexical"`.
- A package's first ranked answer after a load or reload is `retrieval: "indexing"` until its search index is built. A search that runs past 90 seconds answers every target in `unresolved_targets`, with a warning naming a narrower scope to retry with.

For a `dimensional_value` target the judge sees how each field's stored values matched and their scores. Under `egress.preset: "full"` it also sees the values and names the ones it means: a value it was shown and did not name is left out, and it answers no field when no value is the one typed or a form of it. A field offered for a value whose values are not indexed comes with a warning saying they were not checked. Agents are told to scope a value search to its field (`scopes[].source` and `entity_name`) once they know it.

The search index stores the distinct values of `#(index)` dimensions on ungated sources, read once when the package loads, so a `dimensional_value` target matches a value by spelling (and by meaning with an embedding key under `egress.preset: "full"`; under `default` no stored value is sent to the embedding provider or the LLM). A server with no embedding key builds it too, and its ranked answers say `retrieval: "lexical"`. Reads take at most 5 minutes per build. If a value read is refused because the server is at `PUBLISHER_MAX_CONCURRENT_QUERIES`, times out, or is not reached in those 5 minutes, the index serves without those values, and the first question after a cool-down (one minute, doubling each time, up to an hour) reads just those dimensions again in the background. `retrieval.dimensionValues.enabled: false` in `publisher.config.json` stops every load-time value read.

## [0.12.0] — A package agent's skills can ship `assets/`, files the agent copies without reading

A skill an agent declares may hold `<skill>/assets/**`: text files (a chart module, a component library, a template) that the agent copies into what it builds rather than reads. They have their own budget, outside the 256 KB cap on an agent's Markdown, which stays as is. Limits: each file under 1 MiB, at most 4 MiB and 200 files per agent, and 8 MiB per package, a shared directory counted once. `get_agent`'s full view lists them as `assets` (`relative_filepath`, `bytes`, `sha256`, with no contents) plus `asset_roots` (each skill's package-relative directory); the summary view carries `asset_counts`. One asset is served through the existing skill-file route (`skill_path`, `GET …/agents/{name}/skills/{relative_filepath}`), only when its bytes still match the listed sha. Assets fold into `definitionSha` and `sourceContentSha` only when present, so an agent without them keeps both shas. A file that is binary or not UTF-8, too large, over a budget, badly named or a `.malloy`/`.malloynb` file is skipped with a load warning and the agent stays served. A symlink, a path escape, a nested `publisher.json` or `SKILL.md`, `..` in a name or two paths differing only in case drops the agent. **An agent served today whose skill already holds an `assets/` with one of those stops being served** until it is fixed; its load warning says why. The `assets/` directory of a package's own top-level `skills/` is not read. [docs/packages.md](docs/packages.md) has the limits and the trust model: asset code runs unread wherever the app is opened, so review it as code before adopting an agent.

## [0.12.0] — Fields declare their data classes with `#(classification)`, a derived field inherits them, `#(carries)` refuses a surface that exposes more than it says, and the package read summarizes both

`#(classification) "<class>"` on a dimension or measure records the data class the field carries, in the words of the package's access policy (`"phi.direct_identifier"`, `"none"`), or a quoted list, `["phi.direct_identifier", "gdpr.personal"]`, because one column commonly sits under several regimes. Every value is quoted and every list is the bracketed, comma-separated form the rest of Publisher's annotations use, read by Malloy's tag parser: Publisher reads the shape and never the vocabulary. A field that declares none takes the union of the classes of the fields its expression reads, through a copy, a function, an aggregate, a `rename:`, an unclassified intermediate and a join; a declared set wins, with the inputs still reported. `get_context` reports the set as `classifications` on every field card, the source's own fields and the copies reached through a join alike, with `classification_inferred` and `classification_inputs` (the classified fields read, each with its classes) when it came from lineage, and never as description text; two spellings of one column folded into one entity share the classes either declares. The package load gains two advisory findings. `classification-coverage`, once any field in the package carries a class, names every published dimension and measure that has none, one finding per source, following joins three deep and skipping fields behind `private:`/`internal:` and sources locked with `#(authorize) false`; a package that classifies nothing is not warned. `classification-malformed` names a value that is empty, unquoted, space-delimited or does not parse, and a second `#(classification)` on one field, one finding per source naming its fields. Both ride `Package.warnings` and so `get_status`. `#(carries) ["<class>", …]` on a source lists the classes a caller may reach from it, inherited through `extend` like a gate; a reachable dimension or measure with any class off the list, or with no class, is a leak, and a leak **refuses the package load** (400 on publish and reload, a `loadErrors` entry otherwise) with every leak and its lineage named. The load now **refuses a package in which a published source's author-written join bypasses a gate**: an entry source with no gate that joins a source locked with `#(authorize) false`, or an entry whose gates do not read a given the joined source's gate reads, three joins deep, because a gate fires only on the source a query enters through and the joined rows would otherwise reach every admitted caller unscoped; the message names the join and the fix ([docs/authorize.md](docs/authorize.md#author-joins-are-checked-at-load)). And every query-route call now emits one **access record** (`event: "access"`, logger message `Access record`, and `publisher.access.*` span attributes): environment, package, version and model; the source entered, the gates in force and the decision (`open`, `admitted`, `filtered`, `bypassed`); the given names supplied and the ones the row filters read, never their values; every field the compiled query reads with its classes; outcome and status (`ok`, `denied_lock`, `refused_surface`, `bad_request`, `error`), row count, durations, served-from; the trace id; and a `caller` copied from the request header the deployment names with `PUBLISHER_CALLER_HEADER` (default `x-publisher-caller`). A refusal is recorded too, with what the request named. Nothing about the query's answer changes, and a record that cannot be fully built is emitted with what was known. [docs/access-record.md](docs/access-record.md) is the reference. The record reads `#(secure)` givens as the caller's verified attributes and carries their values (and only the names of plain givens), and the load **refuses a package** in which a published source's `#(authorize)` or `#(access_filter)` reads a given not declared `#(secure)`, because a gate a caller can satisfy by sending a value is a filter, not a control. **This breaks packages whose gates read plain givens**: mark each such given `#(secure)` and have the trusted tier set it. Discovery reads secure givens too: `get_context` takes `givens` and `GET …/models/{path}` a `givens` query parameter, and a source whose `#(authorize)` lock cannot admit the caller on the `#(secure)` givens supplied, or reads one not supplied, is omitted with its fields, queries and source info, as a source locked with `false` always was; plain givens and row filters hide nothing, and with no givens every published source is listed as before ([docs/discovery-and-access.md](docs/discovery-and-access.md#discovery-under-a-lock)). None of the annotations changes what a query returns. [docs/classification.md](docs/classification.md) is the reference. Two skills put it to work in a new `governance` group: `malloy-classify` proposes each field's class from the policy's class table and aggregate evidence from the values, as a diff a person approves, and `malloy-compliance-review` turns a policy into a register of checks and runs it with `compliance.py check`, which probes every analytical domain as every role the policy names, fails a field whose values prove more than its class, and exits 1 so it gates CI ([docs/compliance-review.md](docs/compliance-review.md)). The new `clinical-records` example package is a HIPAA worked example of all of it.

## [0.11.1] — A package's load response lists its `#(secure)` givens

`Package` gains `secureGivens`: one entry per distinct `#(secure)` given (`name`, `type` rendered as `Given.type` renders it, such as `string[]`) with the sorted `modelPaths` of the `.malloy` models and `.malloynb` notebooks whose compiled givens surface it, an importing model included. It rides every response that returns a loaded package, the publish (`POST …/packages`, versioned or not), `GET …/packages/{pkg}` and a reload among them, and is read off the compile the package is serving, so a host that sets secure givens no longer compiles the package a second time to learn which ones they are; a reload that changes the models changes it. It is `[]` on a loaded package that declares none. It is absent while any model or notebook in the package fails to compile, and where this server does not report it, so read absent as unknown rather than none. A PATCH body cannot set it.

## [0.11.0] — Packages published from a location can be immutable versions (opt in with `PUBLISHER_PACKAGE_VERSIONING=on`)

With `PUBLISHER_PACKAGE_VERSIONING=on`, `POST /api/v0/environments/{env}/packages` with a `location` publishes an immutable **version** of the package, numbered by the `version` in its `publisher.json`. Every version keeps serving the content it was published with, a request picks one with `versionId`, and a request that names none gets the package's `latest`. [docs/package-versions.md](docs/package-versions.md) is the full reference.

**Nothing changes until you turn it on.** The flag is off by default, and off, every publish from a location installs the package in place and answers 200, replacing the previous publish, as before, whatever its `publisher.json` says. Each such publish logs a warning that versions will be required. The flag is a transition: a future release removes it and requires a `version` ([#1381](https://github.com/malloydata/publisher/issues/1381)), so give your packages a semantic `version` now. Any value other than `on` or `off` fails startup, and `/status` reports it as `packageVersioning`.

**With versioning on, for a publish from a location:**

- A `publisher.json` with no `version` answers 400 `MANIFEST_VERSION_MISSING`, and one that is not a semantic version such as `1.2.0` or `1.2.0-rc.1` answers 400 `MANIFEST_VERSION_INVALID`. Numeric identifiers may carry leading zeros (`01.0.0`); such a version compares equal to the one without them, and a package holds only one of the two, so publishing the other answers 409 `VERSION_CONFLICT`.
- Publishing a version again with the same content answers 200, writes nothing and leaves `latest` where it is, so a retried publish never undoes a rollback. With different content it answers 409 `VERSION_CONFLICT`. **If you re-POST a changed tree under the same version to update it, bump `version` instead.**
- A versioned package no longer changes in place: `?reload=true` (and MCP `reload_package`) returns it as it is (`mode: "unchanged"`), and model, report, dashboard and notebook writes answer 409 `PACKAGE_IS_VERSIONED`, as does a publish to it with versioning turned off again. Iterate with watch mode, then publish.
- `PATCH …/packages/{pkg}` is deprecated, and keeps working so callers that predate versions do not break. Its responses carry `Deprecation: true` and a `Link`, each request counts in `publisher_deprecated_usage_total` (`feature` `package_patch`), and the server warns once per run for each package with published versions, naming `PUT …/versions/{version}/manifest` as the replacement (a package with no versions has no replacement, so it is not warned). On a versioned package it still rebinds `latest`'s `manifestLocation` (a null or empty one leaves the binding as it is; clear it with `PUT …/versions/{version}/manifest`) and sets the package's `description`, and accepts the package sent back whole; a change to content answers 409.
- `manifestLocation` on a versioned publish, on that PATCH, and on the new manifest route is what the manifest loader reads: a `gs://` or `s3://` URI, a `file://` URL, or an absolute path on a mounted volume. A relative path, which would resolve against the server's working directory, answers 400.

A package registered from a directory with no `location`, or published while versioning is off, has no versions and behaves as before. Versions published while it was on keep serving after it is turned off. With versioning on, a package in `publisher.config.json` is published from its location as the version its `publisher.json` declares, by the same rules as a publish, on the first start and on `--init` (the starts that read the config); one that declares no version fails to load, and the others load. A watched environment (`--watch-env`) loads its packages in place, with no versions.

**Reading a version.** Every route that reaches into a package takes `versionId` (queries in the body; materialization create in the body). A version is served; an unknown one answers 404 `VERSION_NOT_FOUND`, an archived one 410 `VERSION_ARCHIVED`, and one that is not a semantic version 400 `VERSION_ID_INVALID`. An empty `versionId=`, and `versionId=latest`, mean no version: the package's `latest`. This holds with the flag off too, and on a package with no versions: routes that used to ignore `versionId` (the package's connections, compile, skills, agents, data apps, events, materializations, and a `versionId` in a model query's URL) now answer a named version 404 and a malformed one 400, and routes that answered 501 now answer 400 for a value that is not a semantic version (`?versionId=v1`). A package listing with a `versionId` other than empty or `latest` answers 400 (it was 501). The deprecated `/projects` aliases that answered 501 to a `versionId` now read it the same way, and so does the `/projects` query route, which ignored a `?versionId=` in its URL (it answered 501 only to one in the body): on a package with no versions, a named version there now answers 404. Responses carry `versionId` and `latestVersion`, data apps carry `versionId`, and `/status` lists every version each package holds (with `includeLoading=true`, a version still being published too, as `loading`, once its `publisher.json` has named it) and reports `packageVersioning` (`"on"` or `"off"`) and `versionPromotion`. These answer in both settings of the flag.

**New routes:** `GET …/packages/{pkg}/versions` and `GET …/versions/{version}`; `PATCH …/versions/{version}` with `{"archiveStatus": "archive" | "unarchive"}`; `DELETE …/versions/{version}`; `PUT …/versions/{version}/manifest`; and `PUT …/packages/{pkg}/latest` with `{"version": "…"}`.

**Archive or delete.** Archiving takes a version out of service and unloads it, but keeps its files, so it can be unarchived. Deleting removes it for good: it is unloaded, its row and its files go, and its version id is free for a new publish; then, in the background, its own running auto-runs are stopped and its own `scope: "version"` tables are reclaimed, as an archive reclaims them; an orchestrated run is left to its caller. Deleting a versioned package cleans up each of its versions the same way. A reclaim tries each table once and leaves one it cannot drop, naming it in a warning. An archived version can be deleted, which is how its files are reclaimed, and deleting a package's only version deletes the package. Neither touches the other versions. Both refuse `latest` (deleting it is allowed only as the package's only version) and the last version in service.

**Promotion.** `versionPromotion` (`PUBLISHER_VERSION_PROMOTION`, or `publisher.config.json`): `on-publish` (the default) moves `latest` to a newly published higher version; `explicit` never does, and only `PUT …/latest` moves it.

**In the Console.** A versioned package's pages carry the version in the path, `/<env>/<pkg>/<version>/…`, with `latest` spelled out, and a bare package link opens `/latest`. A version switch on the package title lists the versions, highest first, with `latest` marked; each row can be pinned as `latest` (after a confirmation), archived (after a confirmation that says what it drops) or unarchived, or deleted (after a confirmation; deleting a package's only version deletes the package). An action the server would refuse is disabled, with why. A pinned version stays pinned through its models, reports, data apps and materializations, and since a published version is immutable its pages offer no report creation or editing, and no scope or schedule. A package with no versions keeps its routes and shows no switch.

**Materializations** build one version at a time, chosen by `versionId`. Under `scope: "version"` each version builds and serves its own tables (`summary__v1_2_0_3f9c2a1b`: the version, and a hash of the environment, package and version, so packages never share them), its runs hold their own slot, and archiving it reclaims them. Under `scope: "package"` the versions share tables: an auto-run of a version other than `latest` answers 400 `VERSION_NOT_LATEST` (while there is no `latest` yet, under `explicit` promotion, any named version may auto-run), and a version binds a stored table only when its own definition built it. The standalone scheduler fires each published version on its own schedule.

**Regenerated clients.** The operations that newly take `versionId` declare it as an optional query parameter after their existing ones, so in a client generated from this spec it comes before the trailing request-options argument: a call that passes options positionally must pass `undefined` for `versionId` first. `versionId` is typed as a string, so a TypeScript client reports such a call when it compiles.

**Upgrading.** An existing `publisher.db` gains a `versions` table and two columns on startup; nothing is lost, and every existing package stays unversioned until its first publish from a location. The SDK percent-encodes `versionId` in resource URIs, so build metadata (`+build.5`) survives.

**Downgrading.** An earlier release starts on an upgraded `publisher.db` and serves every package that has no versions as before. A package with published versions does not load there: its files sit in one directory per version, `<pkg>/<version>/`, and earlier releases read only `<pkg>/`. Delete such a package before you downgrade, and publish it again on the earlier release. An earlier release's `--init` resets the store as before, leaving the `versions` table behind; this release's `--init` removes it.

## [0.11.1] — A dead SSH tunnel no longer crashes the server, and is rebuilt

A bastion refusing to forward to the database, or an SSH session to a bastion dropping, could throw an uncaught exception inside the tunnel's connection handler and crash the server process, taking every tenant on it down. Both are now contained: the local connection closes and the server keeps running. A tunnel that dies is also detected and logged, and the connection is rebuilt on its next query, where before it stayed dead until the environment reloaded or the server restarted. A bastion that closes before the tunnel is ready now fails the connect instead of hanging it. Queries in flight when the tunnel drops fail with a connection error.

**Upgrading: a tunneled connection now runs at most 5 queries at once, and opens a fresh database session for each.** The pool behind an SSH-proxied Postgres connection now matches a direct one. Before, it allowed 10 concurrent sessions and reused them. Now it honours `PUBLISHER_POSTGRES_POOL_MAX` (default 5), so a sixth concurrent query queues, and fails if no session comes free within 30 s; set `PUBLISHER_POSTGRES_POOL_MAX=10` to keep the old capacity. Each query also gets a new session, never a reused one: it opens a new channel through the bastion, connects and logs in to Postgres, and runs the session setup, which adds that connect time to every tunneled query. See [docs/connections.md](docs/connections.md#reaching-a-database-through-an-ssh-bastion-proxy).

## [0.11.0] — A package agent can declare a run budget

An agent in `publisher.json` can now set `budget`: optional `turns`, `wall_clock_minutes`, `llm_tokens` and `job_minutes`, each a positive integer. Set any one of them alone and the rest keep the platform's default. Publisher validates it and serves it from `get_agent` and the agent endpoints, and enforces nothing; a platform that runs the agent may clamp each field to its own maximum. A bad value or an unknown sub-key drops the agent, like any other invalid key. **Earlier releases do not know the key and drop any agent that sets it**, so a package should not use `budget` until every server that serves it runs this release. The new `malloy-define-agent` skill covers writing an agent definition. See [docs/packages.md](docs/packages.md#agents).

## [0.10.5] — A DuckLake storage credential reaches only its catalog's data path

Every DuckLake storage secret (an S3 key, an S3 `credential_chain`, a GCS key) is now created with a `SCOPE` of the catalog's data path: the configured `storage.bucketUrl`, or, when the config leaves it out, the path the catalog recorded at its creation. A `managed: true` connection attached read-only is scoped to its `main` schema's recorded path. On S3, DuckDB's fallback to a key seeded from the host's `AWS_*` environment is turned off on the connection's DuckDB instance. Before, the secret reached the whole bucket, so raw SQL carried into a storage destination's session could read another prefix with the destination's credential. See [docs/ducklake.md](docs/ducklake.md#what-the-storage-credential-reaches).

What can change for a running deployment:

- **A model that read an object outside the data path through a DuckLake connection's credential** (`lake.table('s3://bucket/raw/x.parquet')`) now fails with an unsigned read (HTTP 403 from the bucket). Put the object under the data path, or read it through a `duckdb` connection's `attachedDatabases` entry, whose secret is not scoped.
- **A model on a `managed` connection that read another schema of the catalog** fails the same way; the connection serves `main`.
- **An S3 DuckLake session no longer falls back to the host's `AWS_*` keys** for a read no secret matches.
- **A catalog with nothing to scope to is not attached.** A config with no `bucketUrl` whose catalog records no data path fails the attach, naming the catalog, and the next lookup retries; before, it attached with no storage secret.
- **`S3_CREDENTIAL_CHAIN_POLICY=destinations-only` admits storage destinations on every path** (load, rebuild, serve, build, and the admin API's catalogs); before, a `credential_chain` destination was dropped or refused under the policy.
- **A `publisher` proxy connection to a DuckLake catalog is scoped by the upstream Publisher**, so the upstream must run this release too.

## [0.10.4] — The build plan lists every persist source, with every table it reads

The build plan is computed from Malloy's `Runtime.getBuildTargets` instead of the deprecated `Model.getBuildPlan`. Its wire shape is unchanged, but its `graphs` now carry the whole dependency graph: each graph is a single level holding every persist source in build order, and each node's `dependsOn` names the sources on every table it reads. The graphs used to list only root sources with their direct dependencies, so a host reading them for a rerun's upstream closure, freshness inheritance or lineage lost every edge below the first level. Sources that share a table, a source and its extensions, no longer list each other as dependencies. A persist source whose SQL does not compile on its own (one that reads a `given:` with no default) is refused per source, as before, and lists no dependencies, since Malloy does not report the tables it would read.

Two things to check if you read `graphs` yourself:

- **The one level is not parallel.** `nodes` was documented as levels that each run in parallel, in order. It is now a single level in build order, so a host that builds each level's nodes concurrently would build a source alongside the sources it reads. Order builds by `dependsOn`, or run the level serially.
- **A walk of `dependsOn` reaches further.** A rerun that includes upstream sources, or a freshness rule that follows dependencies, now reaches every source below the first level. Expect such a rerun to rebuild more, and so to cost more warehouse work, than it did before.

## [0.10.4] — A `count()` over a pre-aggregated source counts the source's rows, not the rollup's

A query with an aggregate written in the query itself, against a source with a `#@ preaggregate` rollup, could be answered from the rollup and return a wrong number. `run: orders -> { aggregate: n is count() }` returned the number of rollup rows, and `qty.sum()` with `qty` in the grain summed one `qty` per rollup row. The same held in a `nest:`, a `having:`, and a measure an inline `extend` defined, and on both colocated and `storage=` rollups. A `select:` or `index:` stage was answered from the rollup too, returning one row per grain group rather than the source's rows. Such queries are now answered from the base. A rollup answers only when every aggregate in the query is a pre-aggregated measure or an expression over them. To accelerate a count, declare and annotate it as a measure (`#@ preaggregate grain="category"` on `order_count is count()`). See the "What does not route" section of [docs/preaggregation.md](docs/preaggregation.md#what-does-not-route).

## [0.10.3] — A click on a value opens a menu, and the rows behind it can be shown and downloaded

Clicking a value in a dashboard, a report or a notebook cell now always opens a small menu that says what each entry does, even when there is only one. Before, what a click did depended on a `# drill` tag the reader could not see: one destination navigated or filtered at once, two or more opened a menu, and an untagged value opened its rows.

- **Entries name what they act on.** `Filter to Region: EU` for `# drill { to=self }` (this was `Filter this view`), `Open Regional review (Region: EU)` for each `# drill { to=… }`, and `Show rows (Region: EU, Month: 2025-12)`.
- **A tag no longer replaces the rows.** A tagged value lists its tag actions and `Show rows` side by side.
- **The rows are filtered by every value of the clicked row.** A table grouped by two or more dimensions failed before with "Must provide a value for all dimensions". Refined views, named queries, inline queries and text-source reports now open their rows too.
- **A cell reads as clickable only when its menu lists something.** A tile whose rows cannot be named exactly is not offered rows: a pipeline of more than one stage, an unnamed time truncation inside a view (`group_by: created_at.month`), a row holding a value a filter cannot spell (a uuid, JSON), or a nest whose levels use different time zones.
- **The server corrects Malloy's drill metadata in query results.** A multi-stage pipeline's root no longer reads as `drillable`, a dimension declared in a joined source carries its dotted name as `drill_expression.code` (`users.signup_year`, not `created_at.year`), and an unnamed truncation whose truncation Malloy lost carries no code. A client that builds filters from that metadata now gets the right rows or none, instead of wrong rows. Each corrected result carries a `#(malloy) drill_metadata_corrected` root tag, and the SDK offers rows only when it is present, so a newer SDK against an older Publisher offers no rows rather than wrong ones.
- **Download CSV.** The rows dialog's title row has a button that runs the same query with no `limit:`, so only the server's row cap bounds the file. When the file reaches that cap, its name and tooltip say so.

For SDK hosts: `DashboardView` and `Report` take a new `rowsActions` prop that draws your own actions (an export, a download) in the rows dialog in place of Download CSV; it receives the unlimited query, the givens and a file name. `DownloadRowsCsv` is exported for hosts that want it beside their own. `useDrill`'s `selfLabel` option is removed: every `to=self` entry reads `Filter to <Field>: <value>`.

## [0.10.7] — A same-catalog build of a source that uses built-in functions is no longer refused as author SQL

A `storage=` build of a source that reads the destination catalog's own tables, a pre-aggregate rollup included, was refused with "carries SQL its author wrote" whenever the source used a built-in function (`round`, `nullif`, and others): a function call carries its overload's per-dialect SQL template in the compiled definition, and the author-SQL check walked into it. The check now skips a call's definition and keeps checking its arguments, so an `.sql()` source, a `sql_*` expression (including one passed to a built-in) and a table read from a file or URL are still refused. The refusal's advice no longer suggests dropping `storage=`, which does not help when the source's own connection is the catalog.

## [0.10.7] — A file the admin table load's reader refuses answers 400, not 500

`POST .../tables/{table}/load` on the admin API answered a file DuckDB's reader refused — bytes that are not the format they claim, a value a column's type cannot hold — with `500 Internal server error.`, and the reason reached only the server log. A client that retries 5xx retried the same bytes to the same end.

Now that failure is `400 INVALID_REQUEST` carrying the reader's own words, which name the fix (`Invalid Input Error: No magic bytes found at end of file 'broken.parquet'`; `Conversion Error: CSV Error on Line: 3 … Could not convert string "N/A" to 'DOUBLE'`). The object is named by its file name rather than its staging path, and the SQL DuckDB echoes is dropped. The original, path and SQL included, is logged at `warn`.

Only the reader's statement is classified. A storage or catalog failure (`IO Error`, a flush after the table is written) is still a 500. **If a client retries a load on 5xx**, it now stops on a bad file; a 400 here means the file, not the server, has to change.

## [0.10.0] — Malloy 0.0.436: time-zone reads, refinements that keep their ordering, and booleans on SQL Server

Publisher now builds on `@malloydata/*` 0.0.436, up from 0.0.435. The changes that reach a running server:

- **A query that sets a time zone reads dates and times in that zone throughout** ([malloydata/malloy#3145](https://github.com/malloydata/malloy/pull/3145)). Extraction, truncation, calendar offsets and casts to a date convert the instant to the query zone's clock first, on every dialect.
