Three results can change: a cast between `timestamp` and `timestamptz` keeps the instant instead of consulting the zone; truncating to the hour in a zone with a half-hour offset reads that zone's clock; and a filter on a date column, in a zone east of UTC, reads its day boundaries in that zone.
- **A refinement keeps the view's written `order_by`** ([malloydata/malloy#3136](https://github.com/malloydata/malloy/pull/3136)). A refinement that set only a `limit` dropped the view's ordering, and a view refined by name lost its ordering to the next inline refinement. Both now keep it, so rows from such a query can come back in a different order.
- **On SQL Server, a boolean is a condition and never a value** ([malloydata/malloy#3147](https://github.com/malloydata/malloy/pull/3147)). A boolean used where SQL Server needs a value (a result column, a `group_by`, a function argument, a cast, `=` or `!=` against another boolean) is a compile error at that expression, naming what to write instead, such as `pick 'yes' when is_small else 'no'`. `select: *` leaves a boolean field out with a warning. A filter that compiles to a constant, such as `in` over an empty given, now runs on SQL Server.
- **A SQL Server `datetimeoffset` column is a `timestamptz`** ([malloydata/malloy#3138](https://github.com/malloydata/malloy/pull/3138)), read at UTC or in the query's time zone rather than at the offset it was written with.
- **Importing a persisted source without the given its SQL reads is a compile error** ([malloydata/malloy#3173](https://github.com/malloydata/malloy/pull/3173)). When a model imports a `#@ persist` source whose SQL reads a given with no default, and the model does not surface that given, it fails to compile with `unsatisfied-given-in-persist-source`. Import the given alongside the source. Publisher refuses to build a persisted source whose SQL reads a given, so no built table is affected.

## [0.10.0] — A `where:` across a join to a query source or composite is served when untouched and refused when rebound

A package source whose `where:` read a field joined from a query source (for example `source: pipeline_now is deals extend { where: is_open }` where `is_open` is `deal_first_close.close_type is null` and `deal_first_close` is `duckdb.sql(...) -> { ... }`) was refused with `403 Access denied for source "pipeline_now"`, even when nothing had been modified. Malloy names a query source afresh on every compile, so the row-security binding check could not match the served source against the package's own compile of the same file. It now compares a query source by what it queries, so the same shapes serve whether the query source is joined directly, built on another query source, declared with `extend: { join_one: ... }` inside its own query, built on a parameterized source, or a composite member, and whether the `where:` was inherited across files or not.

A `where:` that reads a field through a joined composite whose members are plain sources (`join_one: cmp` where `cmp is compose(a, b)`) was refused too, and now serves when nothing was modified. Re-joining that alias to a different composite, to a composite in another member order, to one of its members directly, or with another join type is refused. A query source whose base is an inline `extend { where: ... }` (directly, joined into another source, or through a named query) serves when untouched and is refused when rebound. That holds over a table or `compose` base (named, or written inline in the query source), with several `where:` conditions or chained `where:`s, when the source is selectively imported (`import { s } from "mid.malloy"`) from the file that built it, and for the caller's own ad-hoc `where:` on a field the caller defines.

The same check now looks where it did not: inside a query source's base, and inside a join a query stage adds (`run: x -> { extend: { join_one: d is ... } ... }`, a nest's or a view's stage, a query source's own stages). A `where:` there that was written against one field but now reads a different one, because `rename:` or `except:` freed up its name and a later `dimension:` reused it, used to answer with the wrong rows and is now refused with the same `403`. Direct use of such a source was already refused. `/compile` now applies the same inherited-`where:` check as a query, so it refuses a misbound source instead of reporting it clean; a row-level gate is checked only when a query runs. Files whose names need URL encoding (spaces, `[`, `~`) are matched correctly.

An inline `where:` may read a field the same chain defined before it (`extend { dimension: z is ...; where: z }`, or `except:` then a redefinition then the `where:`), including through a join the chain added with `on`; it serves when every field it reads was defined before the `where:` and is refused when any of them is rebound afterwards. That also refuses the restore chain (rebind, `where:`, `except:`, redefine back) and a rebind in the same statement as the `where:`, but only for run targets, a query source's base, and a named query. A plain declared `source: s is X extend { where: ... } { rebind }` is still served, and so are the same shapes reached through a joined source or a stage join. A rebind written entirely inside one query source over an anonymous base (`duckdb.sql(...)`, `duckdb.table(...)`) is served too, as it is on `main` and through a named query: the base is the query's own text, so nothing earlier exists to compare it with. A `where:` written before the `dimension:` it reads, in one block (`X extend { where: z; dimension: z is ... }`), is refused over a **named** base, because the compiled source records no block boundary and cannot tell it from a restore; over an anonymous base it serves. A rebind reached through a field the base itself defines is still refused.

Still refused with `403`, because the check cannot prove them bound:

- a source derived in a different package file from the model being queried, where the `where:` was declared in a file outside the package (direct use, a same-file extend, a caller extend and a same-file query source all serve);
- a composite member that filters its own rows with a `where:`;
- a row-level gate or `#(filter)` that reads a field through a joined composite, and a caller join of a gated source whose gate does: the member Malloy resolves depends on the caller's query, so the gate cannot be shown to bind to the member it was written for;
- an import whose path differs from the file's real name only by letter case;
- a query source over a named base, selectively imported (`import { s } from ...`) from a file outside the package.

If a package that queried through one of these shapes starts returning `403`, look for a source derived with `rename:`/`except:` followed by a redefinition of the name its inherited `where:` reads, or a named base extended with `{ where: z; dimension: z is ... }` in one block (move the `where:` after the `dimension:`).

A `where:` through a composite is evaluated against the member Malloy picks for the query (the first member holding every field used), so a composite's members must hold the same rows; that is Malloy's behaviour, not a rebinding the check can see.

## [0.9.16] — Breaking: the `dashboard_columns` alias is no longer read

Report files no longer carry compatibility with Malloyyo's dashboard format. `dashboard_columns=N` inside the `## artifact` tag no longer sets the grid width; the package warnings name it and say to write `dashboard { columns=N }` beside the tag instead, and the `notebook-columns-alias` and `notebook-columns-conflict` findings are gone. The package-load warning about a `.jsx` or `.tsx` component in `dashboards/` is gone too: Publisher never ran those, and the folder means nothing to it. `kind=`, the query-level `# artifact` and bare-name drill targets were already not read. To migrate, move any `dashboard_columns=N` out of the tag as `dashboard { columns=N }`.

## [0.9.16] — Resize a tile from any edge or corner, with no handles drawn

The Console builder's tiles no longer draw grips on their right and bottom edges. Over any edge the cursor becomes a two-headed arrow, and over a corner a diagonal one: the right and bottom edges set the width and height as before, the left and top edges move that edge and keep the opposite one where it is, and a corner moves its two edges at once. On a report that flows, the first left or top drag places every tile where it is drawn, as a move does. The right and bottom edges stay keyboard controls (the arrow keys step them), and a double-click on the bottom edge still puts a tile back to auto height. A tile of value cards or a table can now be made two rows tall (a chart still needs three to draw its plot), and the cards draw compact to fit.

## [0.9.16] — Arranging a placed report: pack, flow, guides and keyboard moves

On a grid report whose tiles are placed, the Console builder's bar has **Arrange tiles**: **Pack tiles upward** slides every tile up into the space above it, and **Let tiles flow** clears every tile's place and keeps its size, each one undoable edit. While a tile is selected the grid's rows and columns show faintly, so empty space reads as somewhere a tile can go, and Option/Alt with an arrow key moves the selected tile one cell, swapping it with the tile beside it in that direction (so Down past a tile mirrors Up past it) and pushing down anything else it lands on. Placing a report that flowed snaps each tile's edges to the nearest row line, so tiles that touched still touch and none drifts more than half a row. A row of value cards in a tile shorter than it needs is drawn compact (smaller figures, more cards to a row) so it fits instead of scrolling. A host drawing the builder's controls itself gets the same actions as `BuilderControls.arrange`.

## [0.9.15] — Tiles can be placed anywhere on the grid, have heights, and are laid out on their own entries

A tile's entry in `tiles=[…]` can now carry its layout: `"overview -> kpis" { colspan=12 rowspan=2 }`. `colspan` and `break` there win over the view's `# colspan` and `# break` (and `break=false` turns a view's break off), so one view can sit at a different width on each report, and a tile on a view the report imports can be resized at all. `rowspan=N` is new: the tile's height in grid rows of 80px, plus the 16px gaps between them. A chart fills it, a table scrolls in it, and a tile keeps its height beside a taller neighbour instead of stretching to it. Without one a tile is as tall as its result, as before. The manifest's tiles carry `rowspan`, and the lint now reads an entry's `colspan`, `break` and `rowspan` instead of calling them unread.

Tiles can now be placed: `row=N col=N` on an entry put its top left corner at that grid cell. A report with any `row` is placed, so its rows are fixed 80px tracks, tiles sit exactly where they say, and empty space can hold a tile (one can sit under a short neighbour beside a tall one). A placed tile with no `rowspan` is 5 rows (a text tile 2); phones stack tiles top to bottom, then left to right. The lint names a placed tile past the grid's right edge and two placed tiles that cover each other. In the Console builder a move on a grid is now free placement: the first move places every tile where it is drawn, the dragged tile snaps to the cell under it, and anything it lands on is pushed down (a resize pushes the same way).

In the Console builder each tile has a second grip, on its bottom edge, that sets its height in whole rows (arrow keys step it; Delete or a double-click fits the result again). Resizing or moving a tile now writes its layout on its entry and takes the view's `# colspan` and `# break` off, so the layout has one home; an untouched tile's tags are left as written.

## [0.9.15] — Server telemetry: errors logged once by status, new core metrics and trace spans

Operators who alert on Publisher's logs or metrics should read this; nothing in the REST or MCP contract changed.

**Logs.** Every REST error is now logged once, by status: a 4xx at `warn` as `Request refused` with the path and status, a 5xx at `error`. Before, most routes logged every failure at `error`, a 5xx twice, and the materialization routes logged nothing. Errors passed through the error middleware (the concurrency cap's 503, a malformed JSON body's 400) follow the same rule instead of `Unhandled error:` at `error`. The MCP endpoint no longer writes five `info` lines per request; each tool call logs one `MCP tool call` line with the tool, outcome and duration, and transport detail is at `debug`. `execute_query` no longer logs its parameters, which include given values, at `info`. `Serving query from storage tier` moved to `debug` (the routing counter already carries it), `Query parsing error` to `warn`, and the query-path log field that said `environmentName` but held the package name is now `packageName`. An alert keyed on any of these lines needs updating.

**Metrics.** `malloy_model_query_duration{malloy.model.query.status}` gains a third value, `rejected`, for a request malformed before anything compiled. Those were counted as `error`, so an error-rate panel built on this histogram will read lower for the same traffic; add `rejected` to it if you want the old total. The OpenTelemetry resource now reports the real `service.version` instead of `1.0.0`. New: `publisher_mcp_tool_calls_total` and `publisher_mcp_tool_duration_ms`, `publisher_compiles_total` and `publisher_compile_duration_ms`, `publisher_packages{state}` (serving / failed / stale), `publisher_package_reloads_total{trigger,outcome}`, `publisher_connection_operations_total`, `publisher_mcp_row_limit_hits_total`, and `publisher_storage_bindings_withheld_total`. The default OpenAI-compatible embedding provider now records the `publisher_llm_*` metrics the other providers already did. `docs/configuration.md` describes each.

**Traces.** With `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` set, queries are traced as a `publisher.query` span with `publisher.query.execute` beneath it, and compiles as `publisher.compile`, nested under the HTTP spans.

**Embedding provider errors.** Three failure paths of the default OpenAI-compatible embedding client now behave like the other providers: a non-auth HTTP error reports the vendor's parsed message rather than a raw 200-character body excerpt, a non-JSON reply fails without retrying, and a connection dropped while reading the body is retried.

## [0.9.15] — The builder's filter row is in the same order as the reader's

The report builder drew its filter row in a different order from the report it edits. It put the file's own filters first and the model's after them. The reader lists a filter when a tile first reads it, going through the tiles in order, and within each tile it lists what the tile's source reads before the tile's own `where:` bindings. So a report whose model filters every tile by Manufacturer read "Manufacturer, Subject, Recall date" in the view and "Subject, Recall date, Manufacturer" in the builder. The builder now uses the reader's rule, so both show the same row. A filter you add lands where the saved report will put it: after the filters its tile already has. A host that draws its own row for a report should take the manifest's `givens` in the order given, not regroup them by where each given is declared.

## [0.9.15] — The builder says "model" and "tile", not "view"

The builder's text no longer assumes the reader knows tiles run Malloy views. In the chart menu, "From the view" is now **Default**, with "As set in the model" under it. The reasons on greyed-out charts no longer say "view" either, and nor does the text for adding a tile or the New report dialog's. A host's tests that look up these labels or roles by name need the new strings: `Default`, `Search the model`, and the `From the model` listbox.

A filter's menu now speaks of the report's default as well. "Open the report with this value" becomes **Make this the report's default**. Once it is, the menu shows a quiet **Report default** with a check. The button that clears it says **Use the model's default** for a model's filter, or **Use the filter's default** for one the report declares itself, since that one falls back to the default written in the report.

## [0.9.14] — ReportEditor can run its queries at a pinned version while the document stays unversioned

`ReportEditor` takes a new optional `queryVersionId`. The `?versionId=` on `resourceUri` decided two things at once: the package version the builder queries, and the identity of the document being edited (its kept-draft key, its save target, the "pinned version" caption, and the pinned-package save path). A host whose package republishes on every change needs those apart. When it pinned the version, every republish orphaned the kept edits and Save went down the pinned path. When it didn't, Edit missed every result the reader had just cached at that version and re-ran every tile.

With `queryVersionId` set, every query the builder runs uses that version: tiles, the report's manifest, filter options and suggestions, the report listing, and the field catalog. Everything about the document still follows `resourceUri` alone. So a host passing an unversioned `resourceUri` plus `queryVersionId` gets the reader's cached results on Edit, with no second request, while drafts and saving behave as for any unversioned report. A text-held document's compile takes no version, so with `textSource` only its tiles and options follow the prop. When the prop is unset, behaviour is unchanged.

## [0.9.13] — A filter's dropdown can find values past its first 1,000

A `select` or `multiselect` control over a dimension with more than 1,000 distinct values could only ever offer the first 1,000 in order: its options were fetched once, and typing filtered them in the browser, so a value past the cutoff (say "General Motors, LLC" among 2,901 manufacturers) could not be found and no request was sent. Now the suggest asks for one row past its limit, so a cut-off list is known to be one. Typing in such a control searches the whole dimension on the server after a 250ms pause, with a case-insensitive "contains" that every dialect compiles, and offers up to 200 matches. The dropdown says when a list is partial. Lists of 1,000 or fewer behave exactly as before and send no extra requests. This applies to both a package report and a text-held document (`textSource`), since both fill their controls the same way.

A named suggest (`suggest { query=… }`) cannot be searched, because there is nowhere to add the condition to a whole query. Its list is still filtered in the browser; when it comes back at the server's 1,000-row cap, the dropdown says the list is partial and that a value not listed can still be typed.

For an SDK host: `useSuggestOptions` also returns `truncated` (the givens whose list was cut off) and `search` (a server search per searchable given), and `GivensPanel` and `GivenInput` take them as `optionsTruncated` and `optionSearch`. `buildSuggestQuery`'s query now asks for `limit: 1001`, and it takes an optional search text. Hosts that draw controls through `useDocumentControls` get all of this with no change.

## [0.9.13] — Edits put back on opening are said in the save status, not in a banner

A builder that keeps drafts (`ReportEditor` with `keepDraft`, or `ReportBuilder` with `draftKey`) no longer draws a full-width "Restored your unsaved edits from 5:26 PM." banner above the report when it opens on edits kept in this browser. Edits stay kept until Done, so a host that always keeps drafts showed it on nearly every Edit, and it pushed the page down. Now the save status says it: it reads "Draft saved" as before, its dot takes the accent colour, and the first line of its menu reads "Restored your unsaved edits from 5:26 PM" above Discard edits. Once the menu has been opened, or after the next edit, the dot goes back to normal and the line goes back to "Kept in this browser at …". `BuilderBar` and the in-page toolbar both draw it, so a host that draws `BuilderBar` in its own header gets it with no change. The in-page toolbar draws the status only when a draft is kept, so a builder without `draftKey` looks as it did.

A draft kept before the report changed is still asked about on the page, with Restore them and Discard. That warning no longer has a close button: putting the draft back would replace the newer version and dropping it loses the edits, so it stays until the author picks one. An edit counts as picking: the edits replace the offered draft and the warning goes. Before, an edit dropped the draft but left the warning up, and Restore them then did nothing.

`BuilderControls` gains three optional fields for a host that draws its own status: `restored` (`{ savedAt, stale, pending }`, the new `RestoredDraft` type, exported), `restore` (present while `restored.pending`; applies the stale draft) and `dismissRestored` (present while restored edits are news; call it once the author has seen them). `discard` is now also present while a stale draft is pending, as its other answer. Nothing was removed.

## [0.9.13] — The builder's Linear / Grid switch is gone

The report builder no longer offers a switch between `layout=linear` and `layout=grid`, in the Console's bar or in the SDK's `BuilderToolbar`. The builder draws a report in the layout its `## artifact` tag declares and never rewrites `layout=`; to change a report's layout, edit the tag in the file. The switch turned a dashboard into a story (or back) in one click, and the page it left behind was more often a mess than the report anyone meant.

For a host on the SDK: `ReportEditor` and `ReportBuilder` drop the `allowLayoutChange` prop, `BuilderControls` drops its `layout` entry (so a host drawing the controls itself has nothing to draw for it), and the `report.layout_changed` event is no longer emitted or in the `ReportEvent` union. `readReportTagOfText` still reads the layout from any text.

## [0.9.12] — A SQL statement Postgres rejects answers 400 with the database's message, not 502

On a Postgres connection, `sqlSource`, `sqlQuery` and `sqlTemporaryTable` (and their per-package forms) now answer **400** when the database refuses the statement itself: a column, table, function or type that does not exist, a syntax error, an ambiguous name, a type mismatch. The body carries Postgres's own sentence, for example `column "sundance_name" does not exist`. They answered 502 `Upstream connection error.` before, with that sentence logged only on the server.

One case answers **404** instead: a statement naming a table the database does not have (`relation "public.spaces" does not exist`) carries `reason: "TABLE_NOT_FOUND"`, the same discriminator the table lookup has emitted since 0.2.6, so a router that re-resolves a 404 can tell it from a worker that no longer hosts the connection.

If you branch on 502 to mean "the warehouse is unreachable", that is now what it means on these routes for Postgres; a rejected statement is a 4xx. Unchanged: an unreachable database (502, `reason: CONNECTION_FAILED`), rejected credentials (424), a role without `CONNECT` or a table the connection's user may not read (still 502), and every other dialect.

## [0.9.12] — SQL Server connections

A connection of `type: "sqlserver"` reaches Microsoft SQL Server through `@malloydata/db-sqlserver` (Malloy 0.0.435): a SQL login over TCP with `server`, `port`, `database`, `user`, `password`, `encrypt` (on by default), `trustServerCertificate`, `hostNameInCertificate` and `instanceName`, the connector's own field names. The Console's connection dialogs offer it, the schema browser lists the schemas that own a table or a view (`dbo` the default) and a table is addressed `schema.table`. Schema and table names are matched as Unicode, so a non-ASCII name lists under any collation. The password is write-only, as for every other type, and a port that is not an integer from 1 to 65535 fails the config at load, naming the value.

The dialect is experimental upstream; the server accepts it for every compile, so a model needs no `##! experimental.dialect.sqlserver` pragma. The connection is read-only: a colocated `#@ persist` on a SQL Server source is refused at load with the new `RefusedSource.reason` value `read_only_dialect`, and the source serves live. A rejected login answers as rejected credentials (424) and an unreachable server as unreachable (502). A certificate the client cannot verify is neither, since a retry cannot fix it: it answers as any unclassified driver failure on that route does (a 500 on schema and table listing), the server log names the certificate, and the connection test returns the driver's message naming it. A query that outruns `requestTimeoutMs` is likewise not read as an unreachable server.

Not covered yet, as for Postgres in 0.9.7: on the single-table lookup (`…/tables/{tablePath}`) a refused login answers as a plain driver error rather than 424, because the driver returns that failure as text with its code dropped. An unreachable server is recognized there from the text and answers 502, and a table that does not exist answers 404. Every login refusal answers 424, including a transient one such as a paused Azure SQL serverless database once the driver's retries are spent, since the driver drops the server's error number. See [docs/connections.md](docs/connections.md#sql-server-type-sqlserver).

## [0.9.11] — The builder shows the filters a report reads through its model; the skills put a reader's filters in the report

**The builder's filter row now matches the reader's.** A report whose tiles read a given through the model (a source's own `where: Manufacturer ~ $manufacturer_filter`) showed that filter in the reader and not in the builder, which drew only givens bound in the report file. The builder now draws it too, after the report's own filters, in the manifest's order. It can be set, as in the reader, but has no remove badge and no settings: its popover says where it is set and is changed: the model, or a `where:` on this report's own `source:` that applies it to every tile there. Any filter's popover in the builder, a fixed one included, can **open the report with its current value**, written as the report's starting value (`## artifact { givens { … } }`), or put it back to its default; and a filter a model sets offers **Open the model** when the host passes `ReportEditor`'s `onOpenModel(modelPath)` (the Console opens the model's page). `previewGivens` takes the given names read through the model as a third argument (`givensReadThroughModel` computes them), and `FilterEditState` gains `fixed`, the reason a filter cannot be changed here.

**The skills now say where a filter belongs.** A filter a reader picks on a dashboard or notebook (a manufacturer, a date range, a "major only" toggle) is declared in the report and bound on its tiles, and the model's sources are left unfiltered. A given stays in the model only when the data's meaning or access depends on it: a gate, a value every query must supply, a parameter a field is defined with, or scoping meant for every consumer. `malloy-model`, `malloy-reports` (with a before-and-after worked example), `malloy-analysis-report` and `malloy-define` are updated, and an agent that used to put such a filter in the source now puts it in the report.

## [0.9.11] — A required filter asks for a value instead of failing every tile

**A given with no default is now `required: true`** on every given the API publishes (`Given.required`, on the model surface and in a report's manifest). A query that reads one fails until a value is supplied, and a report used to run every tile straight into the compiler's "Given 'RECALL_YEAR' has no value and no default…". Now the reader and the builder run no tile that reads an unset required filter: each such tile says "Waiting for Recall Year.", the page says "Pick a value for Recall Year to see this report.", and the filter's button reads "Required" with a warning edge. Tiles that don't read it run as before, and setting a value runs the rest. A server or proxy that does not send `required` leaves everything running as before.

**In the builder:** a tile with no `# colspan` beside a sized one is drawn as wide as the reader draws it (at least 240px), not one column wide, and its width handle starts from that width; opening a report writes nothing. A report held as text that did not compile, or whose host's `compileSource` refused it, no longer runs its tiles into "Reference to undefined object": they are drawn with "Not run: this document did not compile.", and the problem is said once above the page.

## [0.9.11] — A model's path is in the declared `path` field; hosts own a report's staleness and its drafts

**`GET …/models/{path}` now sets `path`**, the field `api-doc.yaml` declares, which it used to leave null while sending the same value as `modelPath`, a field the spec never declared. A client generated from the spec, or a proxy that re-serializes the response through it, dropped `modelPath` and so had no path at all. Behind such a proxy the builder's Add a tile previewed every view against `models//query` (a 405) and could write an import of `""` for a source the report did not import yet. `modelPath` is still sent, deprecated: read `path`. The builder also no longer depends on either: it uses the path it asked for, so it works behind such a proxy even against an older server.

**`Report` no longer overrides a host's staleness for the `report` key.** Without `manifestStaleTime`, it used to pass `staleTime: 0` explicitly, which beat a host's `queryClient.setQueryDefaults(["report"], …)`, so a host that reads the manifest itself and then mounts `Report` over the same entry read it twice. Now the query client's default decides. With no default that is still 0, so a reader that sets nothing sees no difference. A host whose `QueryClient` sets a global `staleTime` should know that `Report` now inherits it; pass `manifestStaleTime` to fix a value for the reader.

**A host that holds a report as text can give it filters of its own.** `ReportEditor`'s `textSource` takes `compileSource(text)`, the text to compile in place of the document's own. The server's compile refuses a `given:` in held text, so a host passes a function that removes the document's `given:` declarations and `##!` lines and writes each `$NAME` as a literal (`malloyLiteral` and `localGivenSpec` are now exported for this). With it, "Add filter" is on for held text: the editor saves the document's own text, with its `given:` lines, so it stays a report a package can serve, and the builder runs each tile with the filter's value written in as a literal, never sent as a given. `textSource.takenGivenNames` lists names a filter the builder adds must not take (the model's givens, including one only a gate reads), and `DashboardView` takes `literalReads`, the filters each tile reads through values the host writes into its query, which count as read for the "Doesn't respond to" chip and are never sent. Without `compileSource`, nothing changes. In the builder, a filter the report declares that the server has not compiled yet now applies its declared default until a value is set, as the server applies it once the report is saved; it used to filter nothing.

**`BuilderBar` no longer widens a host's header.** Its save status's screen-reader announcer was meant to be a hidden 1px box, but was sized in `sx` units that read as 100% wide, so in a host whose header does not clip it, the page scrolled sideways. It is 1px now.

**`clearReportDraft` and `reportDraftKey` are exported from `@malloy-publisher/sdk`**, for a host that deletes, renames or replaces a report itself and wants the builder's kept edits gone with it. `clearReportDraft({ environmentName, packageName, path })` drops every draft of that report in this browser, on any server and version, and `server` or `versionId` narrow it. `reportDraftKey(…)` is the key the builder keeps a draft under, and `clearReportDraft(key)` drops that one.

## [0.9.11] — A caller's extend of a gated source, or of a model named query, now follows the gate it inherits

A caller who sends `source: mine is orders extend {}` and `run: mine` got a 403 from `/compile` that `/query` did not give, even when the `#(authorize)` lock on `orders` admitted them (#1400). `/compile` now decides it as `/query` does.

`/query` had a related gap that `/compile` shared: a caller-declared derivation through a model _named query_ or query source (`source: mine is q_model extend {}`, `source: mine is gated -> { … }`, a caller join to one) was refused for every caller, including those the gate admits, and a row-gated one never returned its filtered rows. These now admit a permitted caller, with the same rows `run: q_model -> …` returns, and still refuse the rest. An extend of a named query over an _ungated_ source, previously refused, now admits any caller. That is a refusal change: a request that used to answer 403 now answers 200.

A derivation whose chain cannot be proven stays refused: a named query reached through an import, a chain past 64 names, a composite member with a row filter. See [docs/authorize.md](docs/authorize.md).

## [0.9.11] — `sslmode=no-verify` in a Postgres connection string no longer breaks DuckDB attaches

A raw Postgres `connectionString` with `sslmode=no-verify` (the spelling node-pg takes for "encrypt, don't verify") failed to attach through DuckDB with libpq's `invalid sslmode value`. The string is now handed to libpq with `sslmode=require` in its place, for an attached database, a federated source and a DuckLake catalog alike. Queries through the Postgres driver still read the string as written, so `no-verify` keeps its meaning there.

The other node-pg-only URI spellings libpq rejects are normalized the same way: `uselibpqcompat` is dropped, `ssl=no-verify`/`ssl=1`/`ssl=0` become their libpq equivalents, and `ssl` yields to an `sslmode` in the same string. A deployment `PGSERVICE` is treated like `service=`: the service file's sslmode is left alone.

**Deployment `PGSSLMODE=no-verify`** now means `require` on an attach (it previously mapped to `disable`, i.e. plaintext), and is applied to a raw connection string that sets no `sslmode` of its own. A deployment that relied on that to attach a server without TLS now fails the attach; set `PGSSLMODE=disable` or the connection's own `sslmode` for such a server.

## [0.9.11] — A host can theme the report reader and builder to its own design system

**`ServerProvider` (and `ThemeProvider`) take `ui`: the chrome's design tokens.** Radii (control, tile, menu, dialog), control and chip heights, the type scale (page title, tile title, prose, control, caption, label, code), the mono face and the menu shadow, any subset, the rest staying the SDK's. Every report and builder surface reads them from the theme (`theme.ui`) instead of the fixed values it drew with before, so an embedding app such as Credible matches its own system by passing its values. They are the host's, not the server's, so they are a prop rather than part of the `Theme` object. Defaults are unchanged: a host that passes nothing sees no difference.

**Stable class names for what tokens do not reach**, exported as `reportClasses`: the report, its header and title, the filter row, each filter and its popover, each tile and its heading, a clickable cell, the builder, its bar and save status, a tile in the builder and its width handle, the builder's menus, and each builder window. These names are API and kept across releases; MUI's own class names are not.

`CONTROL_RADIUS`, `TILE_RADIUS`, `DIALOG_RADIUS`, `CONTROL_HEIGHT_PX`, `CHIP_HEIGHT_PX` and `TYPE` remain, deprecated, as the defaults. `AppDialog` takes `className` and draws its corners in `ui.radius.dialog`. See [docs/theming.md](docs/theming.md#embedding-matching-a-hosts-design-system).

## [0.9.11] — The builder's windows: Add a tile, Add a filter and Clickable cells, redrawn

**Add a tile** is every view in the package in one searchable list, grouped by source, each by its title and Malloy name with its chart's icon; the arrow keys move and Enter adds. The picked view runs beside it as the tile it would add, with the page's filters, over its Title and a row of only the charts it can take. The Query / Text toggle is gone: **Add text instead** is in the footer. **Add a filter** shows each field's type, offers the control as five pictured kinds (one the field cannot take is greyed with the reason, rather than chosen and then refused), sums up which tiles it applies to until **Choose tiles** opens the list, and previews the filter's button. **Clickable cells** (it was titled Drill) is a switch per dimension, with "Opens … sets …" beside each one switched on. The Add menu and the tile menu are drawn as the builder's other cards.

**New report** is drawn the same way: every view across the package's models in the same searchable list as Add a tile (grouped by source, each group named "<source> in <model>" for a screen reader), a live preview of the one picked, the layout as two pictured cards, then the title and location. The separate Model and First query dropdowns are gone, and a new report's title defaults to the view's name read as words ("By category"). A test that drove those dropdowns picks an option named `"<title> (<view>)"` in the group of that name, and a layout from the "Layout" radio group.

The line under every report saying where Save writes is shown only when it says something out of the ordinary (Save off, a pinned version, a copy that could not be read); the builder carries `data-saves-to` instead, for a host or a test to read.

For an SDK host: `ReportBuilder` takes `renderViewPreview` for the picker's preview (`ReportEditor` passes one); `AppDialog` takes `initialFocus`, a ref focused once the window has opened, since a child's `autoFocus` loses to the focus trap. A test that drove the picker's Source dropdown and "View x" buttons picks an option named `"<title> (<view>)"` instead; one that chose a filter kind from the "Filter kind" dropdown clicks the radio of that name.

## [0.9.11] — Results stay on screen while they re-run, and switching to edit no longer blanks the report

**A result that re-runs keeps its previous answer up until the new one lands.** Changing a filter used to drop every tile on the page to "Running…" and draw it again from nothing; now each keeps its rows, eased back after a moment, with a thin progress bar along its top, and the new rows replace them in place. This is in `useQueryResult` (react-query's `keepPreviousData`), so it holds for every surface that runs a query through `ResultPanel`: report tiles, `QueryResult`, model cells. A host test that waited for "Running…" after a change of givens waits for the new rows instead; the panel is `aria-busy` meanwhile.

**In the Console, Edit and Done swap the page once, drawn.** The page being switched to renders out of sight until its tiles in view show their results, then replaces the one on screen in the same frame, so the report is never blank in between (it was, two or three times, on the way into the builder). The builder's bar comes into the header with it. While both are mounted the page carries `data-switching`.

**In the builder:** retitling, resizing or moving a tile no longer re-runs its query, and a press anywhere off the selected tile or description clears the selection.

## [0.9.11] — The report builder's controls move to the header; a host can place them itself

**The builder's page-level controls are one bar in the header.** In the Console, where **Edit** sits on a report, the builder draws its save status, undo and redo, the Linear / Grid switch, an **Add** menu (a tile, text or a filter) and **Done**. There is no Save button: edits are kept in this browser as they are made (**Draft saved**), and **Done** writes them and shows the report. Leaving any other way loses nothing and no longer asks; opening the report for editing again puts the edits back, with a note and **Discard edits**. Cmd/Ctrl+S still writes without leaving. A test or automation that clicked Save presses Cmd/Ctrl+S, or clicks Done. The page under it is the report as it reads: no toolbar on the title's line, no pencils after every title. Done returns to the report and asks first when edits are unsaved, as **View** did; View is gone from the builder.

On the page itself:

- **Text is edited where it stands.** A title, subtitle, description or text tile takes a faint wash under the pointer, in place of a pencil. A text tile opens in place in the report's own type, with a ring round it, rather than as an outlined box with Done and Cancel under it: leaving it or Cmd/Ctrl+Enter keeps the edit, and **Escape now drops it** (it used to keep it), as a title's Escape already did.
- **The tile menu is a menu**: **Chart**, a submenu, **Clickable cells…**, and **Duplicate**, which writes the copy as a view of its own (`view: by_category_tile is by_category`) right after the original, so its title, chart and width can differ. A tile whose query is written in the file itself, or a pipeline, cannot be copied, and its Duplicate says so. A tile's width stays a drag of its right edge, or the arrow keys on that edge. A choice that cannot apply stays listed, greyed, with its reason under it. The source and view are a caption at its foot.
- **The width handle** is a grip tab at the middle of the selected tile's right edge. While it is dragged, a label says the width it will snap to (`8 of 12 · Two-thirds`), and the columns are drawn as faint bands behind the tiles.
- **A tile moves from its heading and padding**, never from a press inside its table or chart, which scrolls, selects and shows tooltips as it does in the reader.

What an SDK host sees:

- **`ReportEditor` and `ReportBuilder` take `onControlsChange`.** Passed, the editor draws no toolbar and hands its page-level controls over as `BuilderControls` whenever they change (the save status and `save`, `undo`/`redo`, `layout`, the `add` actions, and `exit` when `onExit` is set), with stable actions, and `undefined` when it goes away. **`BuilderBar`** draws them as the Console's bar. Both are exported from `@malloy-publisher/sdk/builder`. A host that passes nothing keeps the toolbar on the title's line, unchanged.
- **Drafts and Done, for a host.** `ReportEditor` takes `keepDraft` (and `ReportBuilder` a `draftKey`): unsaved edits are kept in `localStorage` per report and restored when it is next opened for editing, as one undoable edit. With a draft kept, `onDirtyChange` reports only text still being typed into an open field. `BuilderControls` gains `done` (write, then leave once the write lands; present with `onExit`), `draftKeptAt` and `discard`, and `BuilderBar` draws Done in place of Save when `done` is there. `draftStorageAvailable()` says whether the browser keeps drafts at all, for a host deciding whether it still needs its own leave guard.
- **Escape in an open text tile drops the draft**, and its Done and Cancel buttons are gone. A test or automation that clicked Done presses Cmd/Ctrl+Enter, or moves focus out of the field; one that clicked Cancel presses Escape.
- **The tile menu's Viz type field is gone**: its choices are the **Chart** submenu's `menuitemradio` items, and Drill is **Clickable cells…**.

## [0.9.11] — Server: package loads share the event loop with other requests, queries reuse each model's query model, and a load-phase metric

Package loads and queries do less on the main thread. Nothing an API or MCP caller sees changes: the same plans, findings, warnings and answers.

- Each loaded model builds its Malloy query model once and reuses it for every query, and for the render-tag checks the main thread prepares itself (those the load worker did not reach), where each used to build and drop its own. So does each variant of a model a query compiles against: a row-level `#(authorize)` graft and the storage serve shape. Memory rises by that one structure per loaded model: about 5 MB of heap for the medium generated test package (8 model files) and 14 MB for the large one (24). A cached variant holds one too, and those caches are bounded.
- Render-tag validation, model hydration and the main-thread build-plan derivation yield to the event loop every 10 ms, so a request that arrives during a load waits for at most one step rather than for the whole load.
- A model's report facts are derived once rather than on every query.

**New metric:** `publisher_package_load_phase_duration_ms{phase}`, one sample per stage of a successful load: `worker`, `hydrate`, `render_validation`, `discovery`, `lint`, `build_plan` and `total`. Since 0.9.9 the load worker derives the build plan, so `build_plan` is the time to apply it, or to derive it on the main thread when the worker left it at its soft deadline. `malloy_package_load_duration` is unchanged and still stops before report discovery and the build plan; `total` is the whole load. Each stage is wall-clock time, so a main-thread stage includes the requests served while it yields. Package loads record it; reloads do not. See `docs/configuration.md`.

## [0.9.11] — Reports written as `run:` cells are no longer reports (BREAKING)

**A `.malloy` file whose artifact tag reads as linear and lists no `tiles` is no longer a report.** That was the older linear form: `run:` statements with `(markdown)` notes between them. Publisher stops listing it, its route opens nothing, `GET …/reports/{path}` does not serve it, and the builder refuses to open it rather than converting it. The package names each such file with a new `error` finding, `report-cells-removed`, whose message gives the fix, and the compile check answers the same finding. The file still compiles as a model, so nothing that imports it breaks.

Who is affected: anyone with a linear report written as cells. To tell, reload the package and look for `report-cells-removed` in its warnings, or on the package page. To fix one, rewrite it as tiles: each prose note becomes a named `##|(markdown) name` text tile, each `run:` becomes a `view:` on an extension of its source, and the tag lists them in `tiles=[…]` in reading order. [docs/reports.md](docs/reports.md#files-written-as-run-cells) has the steps, and the bundled `examples/storefront/category-review.malloy` was rewritten this way. The `report-layout-implicit` finding is gone: a tag with no `layout=` and no tiles is now this case. A tag with a misspelled `layout=` (`layout=Grid`) and no tiles is named `report-layout-unknown` instead, and a `tiles` that is not a list (`tiles=foo`) makes the tag unreadable (`notebook-artifact-unparsed`). The replace write, `PUT …/models/{path}` with `expectedHash`, still takes such a file, so it can be rewritten as tiles in place.

What an SDK host sees:

- **`Report` no longer renders cells.** It draws a report's tiles through `DashboardView`, and a manifest that carries cells draws none of them. Two behaviours that were particular to cells go with them: a report's starting `givens { … }` apply without being written into the URL, as a grid's already did; and controls are shown only for the givens the tiles read, so a given only an `#(authorize)` gate reads is the host's to supply unless a tile reads it too.
- **The builder no longer converts.** `readDashboardDocument` refuses a cell-format file with a reason that names the fix. `ReadFailure.legacyNotebook`, `ReportBuilder`'s `conversion` prop, the conversion dialog, and the `converted` flag on the `report.saved` event are removed.
- **`readReportTagOfText` (from `/builder`) can answer `{ status: "cells-removed" }`**, with `unknownLayout` set when the tag names a layout Publisher does not know. Text it used to read as `{ status: "report", layout: "linear" }` (a linear tag with no `tiles`) is no longer a report, so a host that switches over `ReportTag.status`, or keeps its own copy of the rule, needs the new case.
- **`DashboardView` takes `onLinkNavigate`**, for links inside text tiles and the description, as `Report` passes it. Without it, relative links stay as written.
- **`.malloynb` support is unchanged and fenced off.** Its renderer now lives in one folder of the SDK's legacy code, marked deprecated, and a lint rule stops anything else from importing it. `Notebook` still renders a `.malloynb`.

## [0.9.11] — A multi-pick filter keeps the value you just picked when you click away

In a filter that takes several values (`control=multiselect` on a `filter<string>` given), picking a value and then clicking anywhere else on the page removed the value again: the filter read "All" and the query ran unfiltered. The list stays open after a pick so you can pick another value, and leaving it re-picked the option still highlighted, which in a multi-pick takes it back out. A picked value now stays. Text you typed without picking from the list is still kept when you click away, as before. Single-value pickers were never affected.

## [0.9.11] — Reports: one look for every layout, a row of filter buttons, and package problems on the package page

**Every report draws the same page.** A grid report and a linear report now draw the same header, the same filter row, query results in the same cards and prose as bare text, in the reader and in the builder alike. The layout decides only how tiles are arranged: a linear report is one full-width column with tiles inserted between others, a grid has columns and widths. Before, a linear report drew no cards, wider gaps and its own title block.

What an SDK host sees:

- **`GivensPanel` with `layout="bar"` draws a row of filter buttons** (`Category  All`, `Ordered since  Jan 1, 2023`), each opening its control in a popover, instead of a row of form fields. A test or automation that typed into a filter's field now opens its button first: the button's accessible name is `<label>: <value>`, the popover is named `<label> filter`. The `panel` layout is unchanged.
- **`chrome` on `Report` and `DashboardView` is accepted and ignored.** A host that passed `chrome="none"` for a linear report gets cards around its query tiles, as a grid has; text tiles and the description are prose, never a card, in either layout.
- **Report surfaces size their controls and tiles themselves**: 32px controls, 6px control corners, 8px tiles, a 14px semibold tile title, rather than the host theme's button sizes and `shape.borderRadius`. Colours still come from the host palette and the instance theme.
- **The report title is an `h1`.** An untitled linear report is titled with its file name, as an untitled grid already was.
- **The report page carries `data-layout`** (`grid` or `linear`) in the reader and the builder alike, for a host or a test that needs to tell the two apart now that both draw cards. A test that checked a linear report by the absence of cards should check this instead.
- **`Report` takes `manifestStaleTime`**, how long a read of the report is reused without asking the server again (default 0, so a change made elsewhere shows on the next mount). The Console sets a few seconds on the reader it draws while the builder loads, which is how opening the builder reads the report once.

In the builder, a report's filters are configured on the filter row itself: a remove badge on each button's corner, its settings from its popover, "+ Filter" at the end of the row, and a filter no tile reads yet shown dashed and marked unused. The row of chips above the controls is gone.

A tile is removed the same way: a × on its corner while it is hovered, focused or selected, rather than Delete in its "⋯" menu, which now holds the chart and drill only (a text tile has no menu). The last tile of a saved report keeps its × but says why it cannot go.

**Switching from reading to editing no longer blanks the page.** The Console keeps the report on screen while the builder's code and data load, and starts fetching the builder's code when the pointer reaches Edit. A tile the builder has not changed runs exactly as the reader runs it, so it is drawn from the reader's cached result instead of re-running. The builder also reads the report's manifest from the reader's cache entry. `ReportEditor` takes `loading`, what to draw while the report opens (default a spinner), for a host that wants the same.

**The package page says what failed to load.** A file the server could not serve as intended (for example one whose artifact tag still sets `kind=`, which 0.9.8 stopped reading, so it listed under Models rather than Reports) is named with the server's own message and fix. Lower-severity notes are folded behind a count. The Reports heading's create button is now **+ Report**, accessible name "Add report", like every other section's add button.

**Console.** Buttons are 32px with 6px corners rather than pills, cards and menus 8px, dialogs 12px; breadcrumbs are text with slashes. A report, in reading and in editing, sits in the model page's frame: at most 1200px wide rather than 1600px, its title 48px under the top bar like the model's and the package's, so moving between a model and a report does not shift the page.

## [0.9.10] — A gated source author-joined inside a diamond import no longer fails the load as a misplaced annotation

A package whose files import a gated source along two paths — `security.malloy` imports `dims.malloy` and `facts.malloy`, and `facts.malloy` imports `dims.malloy` too — failed to load with `An authorize annotation is never enforced at: on field "<join>" of source "<joiner>"` whenever a source in `facts.malloy` author-joined the gated source. Every file is loaded as its own model, so the gated file is compiled once per import path; the join embeds one parse's gate note while the namespace holds the other's, and the check that refuses a gate typed on a join line told a copied note from a typed one by object identity alone. A copied gate is also a note parsed from the gated source's own `source:` line, so the check now accepts a note at that position as the copy it is. A gate an author types on a join line is parsed from the join line itself and is still refused. A package-scope `/compile` of the same layout now reports clean too; every gate's enforcement is unchanged.

## [0.9.10] — A caller join to a gated query source over an anonymous base is admitted and filtered

A join written in query text to a `#(access_filter)`- or `#(authorize)`-gated source that the model declares as a query source over an inline base — `source: fact is table('…') extend { … } -> { select … } extend { … }`, the usual way a source masks columns — was refused with `403 Access denied for source "<alias>"` (`chain_not_established`), plainly or with an inline pipeline, and transitively through any derivation of it. The resolver anchored the join on the declared source and then insisted on anchoring the source's base too, which an inline `table(...)` cannot be. A query source the model declares is now anchored as itself: its gate entry already carries its base's gates, since query-source derivation is additive, and the query boundary curates it by name. The joined source's row filter is grafted into the join with the caller's givens, its lock is decided, and a hidden one is still 404 under the boundary. A query source the caller writes still has its base walked, and an inline `extend` of a model query source or `sql_select` anchors on the source it extends (Malloy records what a persistable result extends; an inline extend of a table-backed source resolves through the text fallback as before). One consequence under the query boundary: a caller join to an exported query source whose base is unexported used to put the base on the boundary list as well; it now lists only the source the caller joined, which is the one the boundary curates (a `run:` of that source was already admitted). Author joins are unchanged: never gated.

## [0.9.10] — Report builder fixes: a quieter new report, filters that stop covering tiles, tooltips at the cursor

**New report writes less.** A report created from the package page's **New report** no longer starts with an `intro` text tile holding `# <title>` and a line asking for a description. The page already shows the title and offers the description in place, so a new report said both twice. The file now lists only the query tile you picked, and that tile carries `# label="<view title>"`, so it reads "Top products" rather than "Top products tile". Existing reports are not touched. A tool that expected a new file's first tile to be `intro` should stop relying on it.

**The filter bar no longer covers tiles.** In a grid report the pinned filter bar now draws a hairline under itself while tiles scroll beneath it, and leaves a gap, rather than cutting tile headings off at an edge you could not see. A linear report's filters no longer pin at all: there they are a full panel, and pinned they took a third of a laptop screen. This applies to the reader and the builder alike.

**Smaller builder fixes.**

- In a linear report the "+" under the last tile and the "Add tile" button below the list no longer draw on top of each other.
- A tile's menu offers **Drill** only when its source declares a dimension in the report, instead of opening a window that explained why its Apply was disabled.
- While a tile's edge is dragged narrower, the columns it frees show as an empty slot, so the gap reads as room rather than a broken layout.

**Chart tooltips open at the cursor.** A tooltip that opened on a single pointer move, typically a chart scrolled under a still pointer, was drawn in the top-left corner of the window. The renderer recorded the pointer only while a tooltip was already showing, so the move that opened one was lost. The fix is in `@malloydata/render`, and Publisher carries it as a patch to 0.0.435 until a release includes it. The patch applies to the Publisher Console, which bundles the renderer; an application embedding `@malloy-publisher/sdk` resolves its own copy and keeps the bug until it upgrades the renderer.

**Wide tables show their scrollbar.** The Console's thin, overlay scrollbars hid a result table's horizontal scrollbar until you scrolled, so a narrow tile looked cut off rather than wider than its card. Result tables keep a visible scrollbar again, themed for light and dark.

## [0.9.9] — Loading a package no longer holds the server's event loop while it compiles

Loading a package with large models could stop the server answering anything, health probes included, for tens of seconds. The package-load worker compiled the models, and then the main thread compiled them again: to derive the persist build plan, to give the render-tag check a result schema for every annotated query and view, and to build each model's `#@ preaggregate` companion. Several versions of such a package loading together, as on a restart, ran these back to back on the one thread, long enough to fail a Kubernetes liveness probe.

- The load worker derives the build plan, prepares the render-tag queries and compiles the pre-aggregation companions alongside the compile it already runs. The main thread only runs the renderer's check over the prepared results and loads the compiled companions. The plan, and the warnings a load reports, are unchanged.
- What the load worker logs is sent to the main thread as it is written and logged there, naming the package, so it reaches the OpenTelemetry log export along with everything else, even from a load that times out.
- Each load worker keeps the table and SQL schemas it has fetched, so a model's repeated and later requests for the same table no longer round-trip through the main thread. `PACKAGE_LOAD_SCHEMA_CACHE_BYTES` bounds their serialized size (default 16 MiB per worker, a few times that in heap; `0` disables it; a value that is not a byte count stops the server from starting). Entries are scoped per environment and per connection instance, so editing a connection drops them, as it already drops the schemas Malloy caches on the connection.
- A burst of loads is spread across all `PACKAGE_LOAD_WORKERS` workers. Before, every load that arrived while the first worker was still starting ran on that worker, concurrently.
- `/health`, `/health/liveness` and `/health/readiness` answer ahead of the rate limiter and static-file serving.
- A load that follows a timed-out one no longer fails at once on the worker that timed out, which was still exiting; it waits for that worker's replacement.

`PACKAGE_LOAD_JOB_TIMEOUT_MS` still bounds a load's compile, and a load may now run to twice it before its worker is stopped. The work a load worker does for the main thread interleaves with the compile, and the worker starts none of it after three quarters of the timeout. Past that point it leaves the remaining render-tag results and companions to the main thread, model by model, and the build plan, once any model's part of it is missing, to the main thread as a whole. The main thread then does that work as before. A package whose compile fits the timeout still loads, and only one that comes close to it does any of this work on the main thread. A load that hangs is now stopped at twice the timeout. The workers use more CPU per load than before and the main thread correspondingly less, and `malloy_package_load_compile_duration` now includes the work the worker does for the main thread. `publisher_materialization_build_plan_compute_duration_ms` has a `computed_in` label: `worker` for a plan the worker derived, measured from the first model's plan collection to the plan's completion, which other models' compiles interleave with, and `main_thread` for one the main thread derived.

## [0.9.9] - A package can ship its own skills and declare agents

A package can now carry guidance for the agents that work with it. A `skills/` directory at the package root holds agent skills in the agentskills.io format, served next to the bundled ones by a new `get_skill` MCP tool and `GET .../packages/{pkg}/skills`; a package skill with the name of a bundled one replaces it for that package. An `agents` object in `publisher.json` declares named agents, each with a description, an instructions file, its own skills, and optional scheduled tasks. They are served by a new `get_agent` MCP tool and `GET .../packages/{pkg}/agents` and `.../agents/{name}`, listed on `Package.agents`, and shown in an Agents section on the package page.

`get_agent` returns each skill file in full by default; `skills: "summary"` (REST `?skills=summary`) lists each file's name, description and size instead, and `skill_path` (REST `.../agents/{name}/skills/{path}`) reads one file with the same `source` pin.

Publisher serves a definition and never runs one. A client adopts an agent by fetching it and following it in its own session, and the bundled `malloy-run-agent` skill does that when the user names an agent. A definition carries no tool, permission or hook setting: an agent entry with a key this server does not know (`tools`, `hooks` and the like included) is dropped, and a broken agent never fails the package, it is left out with a `Fix:` warning. Schedules are validated (5-field UTC cron, task file in the package) and shown, but nothing executes them yet.

Two things to know when upgrading. `Package` gains two read-only fields, `servedRevision` (minted per load) and `sourceContentSha` (a hash of the model files, package skill files, the `agents` object and every file an agent reads, so it moves on an edit to any of them; a `version` bump, data files and other manifest keys do not). `reload_package` returns both, and `sourceContentSha` unchanged after an edit to a hashed file means the edit never reached the served copy. And the MCP surface grows from eight tools to ten; a client that pins the tool list will see `get_skill` and `get_agent` as new. A package without `skills/` or `agents` behaves exactly as before, and an older Publisher serves a package that has them without the extras.

## [0.9.8] — Reports: one document type, anywhere in a package, with a `layout`

Dashboards and notebooks are now one document type, the **report**, and a report can live anywhere in a package. A report is any `.malloy` file outside `public/` that carries a model-level `## artifact` tag, other than the root `index.malloy`; a `.malloynb` is a linear report wherever it is. `dashboards/` and `notebooks/` are now ordinary directory names: nothing about a file depends on which directory holds it, and a report two directories deep is served like one at the root. Every file served from those two directories before is classified the same way by its tags alone, with one exception, listed under "What may change" below.

A report's **layout** is `grid` or `linear`, decided by its tag: `layout=grid` / `layout=linear`; else grid when the tag lists `tiles` or the file carries a model-level `dashboard { … }` grid tag; else linear. One reader decides it, over the file's model-level notes, whether the file compiled, failed to, or is text handed to the compile check or the save, so every one of them answers the same.

A report is identified by its **path**. Two reports may share a basename in different directories and both are served; the old shadowing (the second file was not served) and the write path's name-collision 409 are gone.

**New routes.** `GET …/reports` lists every report with `path`, `name` (the basename, a label), `layout`, `title`, `description`, `editable` and any load `error`. `GET …/reports/{path}` returns one report by its full package path including `.malloy` (or `.malloynb`), exactly as the listing gives it: the manifest fields for a report written as tiles, or `notebook` (its cells) for a `run:`-cell report or a `.malloynb`. There is no report cell route: a `.malloy` report's `run:` cells run through `POST …/models/{path}/query`, each cell's `text` as the query, the governed endpoint grid tiles already use. `DashboardManifest`, `RawNotebook.dashboard` and a compile's `CompiledDocument` gain `layout`; package warnings gain an optional `code`. The report schemas reference nothing deprecated: `ReportTile` and `ReportCells` are the tile and cell shapes, with `DashboardTile` and `RawNotebook` as deprecated aliases. A write whose rollback itself fails answers 500. Severities are unchanged: every new finding is `warn` or `error`, so a client that accepts only those keeps working.

**Writing.** `PUT …/models/{path}` (the builder's save) now creates a report at any `.malloy` path outside `public/` other than the root `index.malloy` (refused whatever its case), creating missing directories inside the package root only, and replaces only a file the package reads as a report. It still cannot overwrite a model, an untagged file, a `.malloynb` or `index.malloy`. Text whose only `## artifact` is inside a comment or a string is refused with 400 up front, and a link out of the package is refused before anything is read through it. See `docs/security-posture.md`.

**SDK.** `createDocument` (and the New report dialog) writes a new report at the package root by default, so `CreatedDocument.path` is `sales.malloy` where it was `dashboards/sales.malloy` or `notebooks/sales.malloy`, and the template always writes `layout=grid` or `layout=linear` in the tag. A host whose `DocumentStorage` files documents somewhere other than the path asked for (every grid report under `dashboards/`, say) implements the new optional `resolveDocumentPath(locator)`, returning the package-relative path `saveDocument` will really write: the new file's imports are rendered for that path and `CreatedDocument.path` is that path. A store without it is assumed to write where asked; on such a store that relocates files, a new report's imports would not resolve. **Removed exports:** `documentPathFor(kind, slug)` and `documentPathForTitle(kind, title, suffix?)`, which named `dashboards/<slug>.malloy` / `notebooks/<slug>.malloy`, are gone from `@malloy-publisher/sdk/builder`. Use `reportPathFor(slug, directory?)` and `reportPathForTitle(title, suffix?, directory?)`, which name a report's file at the package root (or in `directory`); a host that files reports by kind builds its own path. `createDocument` checks every path it computes, a `directory` included, so `directory: "../x"` or `"public"` is refused before the package or the store is asked anything. `ReportEditor` and `ReportBuilder` take `allowLayoutChange` (default `true`); `false` hides the Linear / Grid switch, for a host that files reports by layout. The Console's builder route is now the report's route with `?edit` (`/<env>/<pkg>/sales/q3?edit`), so a report whose path ends in `edit` opens as itself; `reportEditRoute(env, pkg, path)` builds it, and the package page's `onOpenDocument` default and drafts use it. A `…/sales/q3/edit` link still opens the builder by redirecting to `?edit`, unless a report is at `sales/q3/edit.malloy`. A report under `data-apps/` opens as a report rather than as a data app. The builder reads a file's layout as the server does, from its model-level notes alone, never its folder: `layout=`, else grid when the tag lists `tiles` or the file carries a model-level `dashboard { … }` tag, else linear; a tag that sets `kind=` opens nothing, and the builder names the `layout=` to write. `readReportTagOfText(text)` (`@malloy-publisher/sdk/builder`) gives that answer for any text.

**SDK changes a host must make** (all to APIs the new format introduced or to the storage contract):

- **`DocumentStorage`: a report's path is its identity.** `DocumentLocator.path` (`<env>/<pkg>/<package path>`) is the key: one path is one document. `DocumentLocator.type` (`DocumentType`) is now the report's layout, `"grid"` or `"linear"`, metadata a save records and a listing reports, where it was `"dashboard"` or `"notebook"` and part of the key. Migration for a host store: key documents by path alone, record `type` on save and move, report it from `listDocuments`, and read `"grid"` for an old `"dashboard"` and `"linear"` for an old `"notebook"`. `BrowserDocumentStorage` moves drafts saved under its old type-keyed scheme to their paths the first time it is used, so none is lost. `useDraftType` is now `useDraftLayout`, answering `{ layout, settled }`.
- **The builder's document carries `layout`** (`DashboardDocument.layout`, `"grid"` or `"linear"`) in place of `kind`. Migration: read `document.layout === "linear"` where you read `document.kind === "notebook"`. `SpliceOptions` loses `changeKind`, `modelPath` and `explicitKind`, and `ReportBuilder` loses `explicitKind`: none changed anything any more.
- **`ReportEditor` takes `layout`**, the layout a report opens with (from the listing, or a draft's recorded layout); `kind` still works, deprecated. Once open, the document's own layout decides how controls are drawn, which layout a save records, and which events the builder reports, so they follow a layout switch.
- **`createDocument` takes `layout` only**: its deprecated `kind` option, `CreatedDocument.kind` and `OpenDocumentRequest.kind` are gone, and `newDocumentProblem(input)` takes no kind. `LocatedDocument` has `layout` and no `kind`. Migration: read `layout`.
- **Drill resolves paths only.** `resolveDrillTarget` answers `{ kind: "path", report }` or `{ kind: "unresolved" }`; the by-name arm and `candidates` are gone, and the Console never builds a `/dashboards/<name>` link for a drill. `locateReportByName`, `locateDocument` and `documentRoute` remain, deprecated, for old links only.
- **`Report` renders `.malloy` reports**; a `.malloynb` is rendered by the deprecated `Notebook`, the only component that calls the deprecated notebook routes. The Console routes a `.malloynb` there.
- `reportRoute` encodes the environment and package names as well as the path, so no caller encodes them again.

**Server telemetry, renamed outright (no dual emission).** Dashboards to update:

- `publisher_dashboard_writes_total` → `publisher_report_writes_total`, and `publisher_dashboard_write_duration_ms` → `publisher_report_write_duration_ms`. The `kind` label is now `layout` (`grid`/`linear`); `outcome` keeps its values and gains `rollback_failed` (a write whose restore failed too, so the package may serve either text); the counter gains `reason`, why a write did not land (`frozen_config`, `invalid_path`, `missing_source`, `untagged`, `not_a_report`, `conflict`, `compile_failed`, `not_found`, `reload_failed`, `bad_request`, `other`; `none` when it did).
- `publisher_notebook_discovery_total` is removed. Discovery is now counted for reports of both layouts: `publisher_reports_discovered_total{layout}`, `publisher_report_files_total{status}` (`served`, `tileless`, `invalid`, `dropped`) and `publisher_report_lint_findings_total{code,severity}`, once per load or reload, with `publisher_report_discovery_duration_ms{during}` (`load`, `reload`, `compile`) timing every pass. A notebook whose cells the reader refused, its old `outcome="refused"`, is `publisher_report_lint_findings_total{code="notebook-cells-unreadable"}`; a `.malloynb` load is `publisher_deprecated_usage_total{feature="malloynb"}`.
- New: `publisher_report_read_duration_ms{route,status_class}` for `GET …/reports` (`list`) and `GET …/reports/{path}` (`get`), and `publisher_deprecated_usage_total{feature}`, one per use of a deprecated feature: the legacy routes (`dashboards_list`, `dashboard_get`, `notebooks_list`, `notebook_get`, `notebook_cell`), the Console's `/dashboards/<name>` alias (`console_alias`), and per load or reload a `.malloynb` file (`malloynb`), a package setting `explores` or `queryableSources` (`explores`, `queryable_sources`), a source declaring `#(filter)` (`filter_annotation`), and a query sending filter values or a bypass (`filter_params`, `bypass_filters`). It is the evidence for when each can go.
- `publisher_notebook_cell_executions_total` and `publisher_notebook_cell_execution_duration_ms` are unchanged; they measure the deprecated cell route only.

Logs: report lint findings are no longer logged at `warn` on every load, reload and metadata change. Each load or reload logs one `info` line, `Report discovery`, with the package, `during`, the counts by layout and status, and the findings by code; each finding is a `debug` line, `Report lint finding`, with `code`, `severity` and `model`. Report discovery and write log lines name the file `model` (was `modelPath`) and the failure `error` (was `detail`). A rolled-back write is logged once (`Report write rolled back`, `warn`), and a failed rollback once at `error` (`Report write rollback failed`) with both `error` and `restoreError`; a refused write is `Report write refused` at `warn`. A 4xx on the report and legacy report routes is logged at `warn`, not `error`.

**SDK telemetry, renamed outright (no dual emission).** Every report surface reports one event family, `ReportEvent`, through the `onEvent` props it already had, and every event carries the report's package `path` and its `layout` (`grid`/`linear`; absent only on a `report.load_failed` that happened before the report said). The host adds the environment and package when it logs, as before.

- **Removed SDK types:** `DashboardEvent`, `DashboardEventHandler`, `NotebookEvent`, `NotebookEventHandler`, `BuilderEvent`, `DocumentCreatedEvent`, `DashboardCreatedEvent` and `NotebookCreatedEvent`. Use `ReportEvent` and `ReportEventHandler` (both entries), with `ReportEventContext`, `ReportFailure`, `DrillOutcome` and `SavesTo`.
- **Renamed events:** `dashboard.opened` / `notebook.opened` → `report.opened` (`surface: "edit"`; `cells` is now `tiles`); `dashboard.open_refused` / `notebook.open_refused` → `report.load_failed` with a `category` (`not_found`, `forbidden`, `invalid`, `unsupported`, `server`, `network`, `unknown`) and no `reason`, since the message can carry a path or a value; `dashboard.saved` / `notebook.saved` → `report.saved` (`cells` → `tiles`; `converted` is present only when true); `*.save_refused`, `*.save_undone`, `*.save_undo_refused` → `report.save_refused`, `report.save_undone`, `report.save_undo_refused`; `dashboard.created` / `notebook.created` → `report.created` (now with `durationMs`); `dashboard.rows_shown` → `report.rows_shown`; `dashboard.explored` → `report.explored`. Migration: match on the `report.*` name and read `layout` where you read the `dashboard.`/`notebook.` prefix.
- **New events:** `report.opened` and `report.load_failed` from `Report` itself (`surface: "view"`), once per report shown, for grid, linear and `run:`-cell reports alike, where before only a grid report's rows dialog reported anything; `report.query_failed` (`tile` index, `category`) for a tile or cell whose query failed; `report.create_refused` (`reason`) for a create that did not land; `report.layout_changed` (`from`, `to`) when an author switches Linear/Grid; `report.drill` (`to: "self" | "report"`, `outcome: "resolved" | "unresolved" | "malformed"`).
- **Prop changes:** `Report`'s `onNavigate` may return a `DrillOutcome`, which `Report` reports as `report.drill`; returning nothing reports nothing. `Package` takes `onEvent` and passes it to its New report dialog. `DashboardView` no longer takes `onEvent`: it reports through the `Report` (or deprecated `Dashboard`) that renders it. Inside a `Report`, a failed cell and a refused `to=self` drill go to `onEvent` and are no longer logged to the browser console; without an `onEvent` they still are.
- **Console:** every event is one log line under `[publisher.report]` (was `[publisher.dashboard]` and `[publisher.notebook]`), at `warn` for a failure (`load_failed`, `query_failed`, any `*_refused`, a failed `rows_shown`, a drill that did not resolve) and `info` otherwise.
- **A host with an event sink must update it** before taking this SDK. Credible's draft editor matches `dashboard.saved`, `notebook.saved`, `dashboard.save_undone`, `notebook.save_undone`, `dashboard.created` and `notebook.created`, and imports `BuilderEvent`; it needs `report.saved`, `report.save_undone` and `report.created`, and `ReportEvent`.

**Deprecated, still working until a later release removes them:**

- `GET …/dashboards` and `…/dashboards/{name}` (the grid reports) and `GET …/notebooks`, `…/notebooks/{path}` and `…/cells/{i}` (the linear reports). `…/dashboards/{name}` resolves a basename only when exactly one grid report has it, and answers 409 naming every match when several do. Move to `…/reports`.

  These deprecated routes still answer, but their contracts are wider than before, and a client of them should check:
  - `GET …/dashboards/{name}` can now answer **409** (several grid reports share the basename). It never did before. The package warns about each such basename at load (`report-name-ambiguous`, `warn`, naming the paths); fix it by renaming one of the files.
  - `GET …/dashboards` and `GET …/notebooks` now list reports from **anywhere** in the package, not only files directly under `dashboards/` or `notebooks/`: a `path` may be `sales/q3.malloy` or `a/b/c.malloy`, and a grid report in `notebooks/` is listed by `…/dashboards`, a linear one in `dashboards/` by `…/notebooks`.
  - `Dashboard.name` is still the basename, but it is **no longer unique** in the listing; key on `path`.
  - The SDK's `DrillNavigation.path` (what a `# drill` click hands a host; `dashboard` before, see below) is the tag's `to=`, which is now usually a **path containing `/`** (`sales/overview`) rather than a single-segment slug. Resolve it with `resolveDrillTarget` against `GET …/reports` rather than putting it into a URL as one segment.

- **SDK names that said "dashboard" for a report**, renamed with the old names kept as deprecated aliases, removed with the other deprecated APIs. Migration: import the new name; nothing else changes.
